Ristorante Raimondi opens onto the shore — request a balcony room on the upper floors for the full western reach of the lake. The view here is why it holds our certification.
Description ⚙: This restored 19th century villa is set on the western shores of Lake Como, between Cernobbio and the town of Como. It offers elegant rooms with parquet floors and marble bathrooms. Set in a private park with orange and lemon groves, the historic Hotel Villa Flori features Venetian stucco work and frescos. The Italian general Giuseppe Garibaldi got married here. All air-conditioned rooms provide flat-screen satellite TV and a mini-bar. Some rooms feature a balcony and lake views. Restaurant Raimondi enjoys panoramic lake views, and serves an eclectic mix of international and local cuisine for both lunch and dinner. Villa Flori lies close to the town of Como and features a private dock for guests arriving by boat.

Hotel Tagline: Facing Bellagio across the water, the floating pool puts the full lake panorama at surface level.
Summary: Established in 1910, this Art Nouveau palace faces Bellagio across the lake. The floating pool sits directly on the water — the most efficient way to take in the full panorama. We’d ask for the Suite Greta or a rooftop suite for the view above the treetops.
Description ⚙: The Grand Hotel Tremezzo, perched elegantly on the shores of Lake Como, presents a spectacle of luxury with its impressive views over the lake and Bellagio. This lavish lakefront property, established in 1910 as a haven for Belle Époque socialites, continues to exude old-world glamour and grace. Renowned for its opulent interior design, the hotel blends classic and contemporary styles with select suites offering private terraces. The historic Suite Greta pays homage to the illustrious guest Greta Garbo, who fell in love with its sunny lake and mountain vistas. The hotel's iconic floating pool is set on the waters of Lake Como, providing guests with an unforgettable swimming experience with views including the picturesque town of Bellagio on the opposite margin. Guests can relax at the multi-award-winning T Spa in the historic Villa Emilia, complete with treatment rooms, an infinity pool, a hammam suite, and steam rooms. Culinary delights await at La Terrazza Gualtiero Marchesi restaurant, the only restaurant in Italy serving the complete tasting menu of the late maestro. Da Giacomo al Lago offers a scenic seafood dining experience by the lake adjacent to the floating pool deck.
Address: Via Statale, 5401, 22019 Tremezzina CO, Italy
Nearest Airports: LUG · Lugano · 40 km

Description ⚙: The Mandarin Oriental, Lago di Como, skilfully intertwines historical charm with contemporary luxury on the picturesque shores of Lake Como. It is housed in the 19th-century Villa Roccabruna and features 75 rooms and suites across multiple categories, including two private villas — Villa del Lago and Villa della Rocca. The hotel elevates its offerings with a 40-metre infinity floating pool, designed by Herzog and de Meuron and the largest on the lake, positioned directly on the water. The renovated Spa & Wellness oasis features six treatment rooms, two private Spa Suites, a zen garden, and a redesigned wet area overlooking the lake. The hotel boasts L'ARIA, offering refined Italian cuisine with Japanese influences under Chef Massimiliano Blasone, and the CO.MO Bar & Bistrot for casual lakeside dining. Committed to sustainability, the resort sources 100% of its energy from renewable sources and provides fully electric vehicles for guest use.
Address: Via E. Caronti, 69, 22020 Blevio CO, Italy
Nearest Airports: LUG · Lugano · 40 km; MXP · Malpensa · 54 km

Summary: Eighteen suites in the center of Como, at the southernmost point of the lake. The Infinity Bar is the clearest reason to arrive before sunset — a cocktail terrace with a full lake panorama, above the ferry terminal. Upper-floor suites add the view from the room.
Description ⚙: Vista Palazzo is located in the heart of Como's city center, a short distance from the ferry terminal, at the southernmost point of Lake Como. The hotel features 18 elegantly designed suites and rooms, each offering a unique combination of luxury and comfort. The suites are spacious and equipped with king beds and magnificent windowed marble bathrooms. All rooms offer an outstanding view of Lake Como from its southernmost point. The Infinity Bar is a panoramic rooftop cocktail terrace with a full lake vista above the ferry terminal, a destination in its own right for non-guests. The hotel's restaurant, Sottovoce, proposes a journey across contemporary Italian cuisine through a tasting menu. Guests can enjoy private transfers, motorboat rentals, a personal butler service, and in-suite spa treatments.
Address: Piazza Camillo Benso Conte di Cavour, 24, 22100 Como CO, Italy
Nearest Airports: LUG · Lugano · 34 km; MXP · Malpensa · 48 km; LIN · Linate · 69 km

Hotel Tagline: Where the lake divides into two, both arms stretch out below at once.
Summary: At the tip of Bellagio’s promontory, where the two arms of the lake divide, this 1873 grande dame overlooks both branches at once. Mistral, the Michelin-recognized restaurant led by Chef Ettore Bocchia, sits on a veranda above the water. The hotel joined Relais & Châteaux in July 2025.
Description ⚙: Showcasing spectacular views over Lake Como, the Italian Alps, and Bellagio, the Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni has been in the Bucher family for four generations. Situated at the tip of Bellagio's promontory where the two arms of the lake divide, the hotel provides simultaneous views over both branches of the lake. With indoor and outdoor swimming pools, immaculately landscaped gardens, and a sublime spa and beauty salon, the hotel belongs to the elite of the finest hotels in Lake Como. Its interior décor features timeless carpeted floors, antique furniture, frescoed ceilings, opulent staircases, a grand hall, and magnificent chandeliers — all nodding to the history of the building that stems as far back as 1873. The hotel's Michelin-recognized Mistral restaurant, led by executive chef Ettore Bocchia (Italy's leading molecular gastronomist), offers fine dining on a veranda above the water. La Goletta restaurant serves gourmet Italian cuisine on a terrace by the pool. In July 2025 the hotel joined Relais & Châteaux, becoming the first and only property on Lake Como in that collection.
Address: Via Teresio Olivelli, 1, 22021 Bellagio CO, Italy

Hotel Tagline: Floor-to-ceiling windows frame Lake Como and the Alpine scenery beyond.
Summary: Opened in 2016, Il Sereno’s suites were designed by Patricia Urquiola with floor-to-ceiling windows — the lake is the room’s primary element. The 1-Michelin-star restaurant Al Lago, led by Chef Raffaele Lenzi, reinforces the argument. Worth timing a stay for a sunset dinner on the terrace.
Description ⚙: Since its opening in 2016, Il Sereno Lago di Como has been fabulously positioned along the shores of Lake Como, only a 15-minute drive from the charming town of Como. The fashionable hotel features elegantly designed suites by Patricia Urquiola, showcasing modernist Italian style with natural materials like Canaletto walnut, Verde Alpi stone, and Venetian terrazzo floors. Expansive floor-to-ceiling windows offer hypnotic views of Lake Como and the Alpine scenery, a perk available across all the hotel's chic suites. The seasonal outdoor infinity pool overlooks the lake. Culinary delights await at Il Sereno Al Lago restaurant, which holds one Michelin star under Executive Chef Raffaele Lenzi, a romantic lake vista enhancing the flavours of contemporary Italian cuisine with global influences. The hotel has a small sandy beach with direct lake access and water activities including paddle boarding, kayaking, and rowing. A spa housed in a former boathouse is also available. Guests can take one of the iconic Riva speedboats from the private dock for a spin around the lake.
Address: Via Torrazza, 10, 22020 Torno CO, Italy

Summary: Twelve keys, no more. The Grand Suite earns the most direct lake view, with Isola Comacina reading clearly across the water. Arriving by boat to the private dock — with the white villa appearing from the lake — sets the right tone. GAIA Bar handles the rest.
Description ⚙: Nestled along the pristine waters of Lake Como, the luxurious MUSA Lago di Como stands as a beacon of modern architecture and seclusiveness. This elegant, white-hued villa offers no more than 12 exclusive keys, each unlocking spotless accommodations with a balcony with stunning views of the lake's charming scenery, including Isola Comacina — the only island on Lake Como. For the best possible views and extra space, the gorgeous Grand Suite is recommended. Guests are treated to pristine white linen bedding, tasteful contemporary art, and luxurious white marble bathrooms with deep bathtubs and spacious showers. Accessible either by a scenic drive from the town of Como or by boat, arriving at its private dock, the villa offers a serene getaway. The decor is a testament to minimalist elegance, with a palette of neutrals and blacks. Culinary experiences are a highlight, with meals served in the glass-encased dining room or on the terrace. The GAIA Bar serves signature cocktails named after notable women alongside extraordinary lake views.
Address: Via Statale, 45, 22010 Sala Comacina CO, Italy
Nearest Airports: LUG · Lugano · 52 km; MXP · Malpensa · 70 km

Hotel Tagline: Rooms in the Casa al Lago sit where the water fills the view.
Summary: An 18th-century villa opened as a hotel in 2022, with 24 rooms across three buildings in Moltrasio. The Casa al Lago rooms sit closest to the water — those are the ones to request. Dinner is served anywhere on the property; the terrace above the lake is where most evenings land.
Description ⚙: Passalacqua, located in the comune of Moltrasio, opened its doors for the first time in 2022 in a beautifully restored 18th-century private dwelling. The exclusive hotel melds historic charm with luxurious amenities, offering guests an experience of antique elegance in a modern setting. This boutique hotel spreads charm across 24 uniquely designed rooms and suites distributed over three main buildings: the Villa, the Palazz, and the Casa al Lago. The Villa features twelve opulent rooms ranging from double rooms to grand suites, while the Casa al Lago offers four rooms with stunning lake views, perfect for couples or those seeking privacy. The hotel's culinary experience focuses on the simplicity and authenticity of Italian cuisine, made from local, seasonal ingredients. Guests have the flexibility to dine anywhere on the property, including the romantic terrace above the lake. The pool terrace is among Passalacqua's most celebrated features. For wellness and relaxation, the hotel offers a spa and wellness center housed in the Palazz, known as the Sottoterra — a hidden gallery made of stones under the property's gardens.
Address: Via Besana, 59, 22010 Moltrasio CO, Italy
Nearest Airports: LUG · Lugano · 37 km; MXP · Malpensa · 55 km

Hotel Tagline: Bellagio sits across the water, visible from every lake-facing balcony.
Summary: A former wire factory in Lezzeno, now a contemporary hotel with an infinity pool that extends over the lake. Bellagio reads clearly on the opposite shore. Request a lake-view junior suite — every room has a balcony — and consider arriving by water taxi for the right approach.
Description ⚙: Many of Lake Como's hotels are palatial villas or neoclassical mansions, but Filario Hotel & Residences is housed in a former wire factory in Lezzeno — midway between Bellagio and Como on the eastern shore — that has been cleverly converted into a luxury hotel with an infinity pool and a private beach. Industrial-chic is the style: cool stone and glass that lets in abundant natural sunlight, as well as views of the lake. Guest rooms are elegant and minimalist, with natural wood paneling, white linens, slate bathrooms, and a private terrace or balcony facing the water; Bellagio is visible on the opposite shore. All 13 hotel rooms have lake-view balconies. The property also includes 22 residences with fully equipped kitchens. The infinity pool extends directly over the lake. Restaurant Filo serves seasonal Italian cuisine on a lakeside terrace for lunch and fine dining at dinner. The beach bar and bistrot Yeast provides casual meals and gourmet pizza at the private black-sand beach alongside a private marina. Filario is listed in the Michelin Guide and is a Design Hotels member.
Address: Località Bagnana, 96, 22025 Lezzeno CO, Italy
Nearest Airports: LUG · Lugano · 56 km; MXP · Malpensa · 70 km

Hotel Tagline: From the rooftop, Como spreads below and the mountains rise across the water.
Summary: The rooftop infinity pool at Terrazza 241 is the view argument for the Hilton — a lake panorama from above the city, with Como spread below and the mountains across the water. Lake View suites add a private terrace and a hot tub. The pool is the reason to stay.
Description ⚙: Just steps from the shores of Lake Como, Hilton Lake Como welcomes guests year-round with a sophisticated atmosphere and breathtaking views. The crown jewel is Terrazza 241, the rooftop infinity pool where guests can sip cocktails at sunset and enjoy gourmet cuisine from lunch through dinner with a stunning lake and mountain backdrop. Inside, the Satin restaurant features seasonal and rotating culinary concepts, and Taffeta Bar provides relaxed elegance throughout the day. The rooms combine style and elegance with warm parquet floors and modern comforts. Some rooms offer the luxury of a private terrace with spectacular lake views or an outdoor whirlpool. The eforea spa and health club is the ideal place to recharge, featuring a hydrotherapy pool, Finnish sauna, Turkish bath, whirlpool, solarium, and a fully equipped fitness centre. The hotel is the first Hilton in the Lake Como region, located 500 metres from Villa Olmo and approximately 15 minutes on foot from Como's ferry terminal.
Address: Via Borgo Vico, 241, 22100 Como CO, Italy

Hotel Tagline: Windermere begins at the garden's edge and fills every window from there.
Summary: The only hotel on Windermere’s eastern shore, sitting in the water rather than overlooking it. Reopened November 2023 after a full restoration. The Boathouse suite hovers over the lake on its own jetty — floor-to-ceiling glass, dual copper baths, private rooftop terrace.
Description ⚙: Langdale Chase holds something no other hotel on Windermere can claim: it stands directly on the lake's eastern shore, its 1890 Victorian stonework reflected in the water at the bottom of its own gardens. The Grade II listed property reopened in November 2023 following a careful, multi-million-pound restoration and within five months had been awarded five AA stars and The Times' North Hotel of the Year 2024. The 30 rooms and suites are split across the main house, the adjoining Lakehouse, and a private Boathouse — all but two with direct lake views. The Boathouse suite takes this to its logical extreme: hovering over the lake on its own jetty, with floor-to-ceiling glass, dual copper bathtubs, and a private rooftop terrace. The two-AA-Rosette Dining Room features walls of glass that hold Windermere in frame from the first course to dessert. A 1928 teak-and-mahogany motor yacht, Albatros, offers private lake cruises from the hotel's own jetty.
Address: Ambleside Road, Ecclerigg, Windermere LA23 1LW, UK
Nearest Airports: CAX · Carlisle Lake District · 88 km

Description ⚙: The five-star Lido Palace hotel lies a pleasant stroll away from the charming little town of Riva del Garda, in Lake Garda's northernmost location. As one of the best hotels in Lake Garda, it is a beacon of lakeside luxury and elegance. At first glance, it is the Belle Époque facade, artistically reenvisioned by the Venetian architect Alberto Cecchetto, that captivates; however, it is from inside that a beauty overload takes place in the form of astonishing lake views. The exclusive hotel boasts forty-two meticulously designed rooms and suites. These accommodations range from the expansive Sky Presidential Suite to the cozy single rooms, all characterized by their elegant design and attention to detail. The rooms and suites come in twelve different types, ensuring a variety of experiences for guests, from breathtaking lake views to tranquil garden vistas. Among our favorites are the Terrace Studios, which offer a panoramic outdoor balcony facing the Garda Prealps, as well as a waterside view. For those seeking culinary delights, the hotel offers a gourmet breakfast — lake view included, especially from the ample terrace — and three distinct dining venues: fine-dining Il Re della Busa, the more relaxed Tremani Bistrot for lunch and dinner, and the Balì Bar for cocktails and light bites. Lido Palace is also home to the CXI Spa, a 1,500 m² wellness sanctuary that blends luxury, beauty, and nature with self-care traditions from around the world. This vast area includes a 24/7 fitness center equipped with Technogym machines, two pools (indoor and outdoor), and a Finnish sauna.

Description ⚙: For those looking to heal their body and soul while being immersed in dramatic scenery, the Lefay Resort & Spa Lago Di Garda is the ultimate choice. Starting with the obvious, the panoramic pool, suspended between Italy's largest lake and the sky surrounded by limestone mountains, is the hotel's welcome card. The commanding views of the Riviera dei Limoni below trigger guests into contemplation mode, preparing them for a stay that holds firm on the promise of delivering a renovated state of mind. The award-winning spa offers health-focused programs and wellness treatments that seamlessly blend Traditional Chinese Medicine with the most cutting-edge techniques from Western science. Apart from that, guests are invited to take the most out of six on-site saunas, a sprawling salt lake, an infinity pool, a steam room, an ice pool, a whirlpool tub, and indoor and outdoor heated pools. The Royal Pool & Spa Suite, the most impressive accommodation at Lefay Resort & Spa Lago Di Garda, not only boasts stunning lake views but also features a private infinity pool, a private spa, and all the amenities demanding guests can expect from such a luxurious suite. Also impressive are the hotel's Sky Suites, offering private terraces with expansive lake vistas and outdoor Jacuzzi. In conjunction with the fabulous views, the high-end hotel treats its patrons with the healthiest take possible on the Mediterranean diet. The Gramen restaurant — a plant-based and fish-focused fine-dining venue with a panoramic terrace overlooking the lake — and La Limonaia, the resort's main restaurant serving Mediterranean-inspired cuisine, complete the culinary offering.

Summary: Opened in summer 2023, perched 200 metres above the lake’s eastern shore and still drawing some of the highest guest satisfaction scores on Garda. We’d book the Deluxe Sky Pool Suite — rooftop terrace, private infinity pool, the lake laid flat below.
Description ⚙: Sharing the same DNA of luxury and secludedness as its sister property, Alpiana, in South Tyrol, the Margesin family raised the stakes at Lake Garda's Cape of Senses, a cross between a boutique hotel and a lavish spa resort. The stunning high-end property, perched 200 meters above the lake's eastern shore, opened its doors in the summer of 2023, and ever since, guests — especially couples — have been reporting stratospheric satisfaction levels. A limited number of 55 elegantly designed suites host those looking for the ultimate relaxation getaway on the Veneto side of the lake. All accommodations are dominated by wood elements and have been envisioned to deliver absolute serenity and maximize the connection between guests and the stunning surrounding landscape. The epitome of this vision takes the form of the Deluxe Sky Pool Suite, especially for guests contemplating the lake vistas from an expansive terrace on the rooftop, complete with a private infinity pool. Apart from its hypnotic views, the major highlight of Cape of Senses is its 2,000 m² Senses Spa, designed by the talented team of DemetzArch and inspired after the senses of smell, touch, taste, and hearing. The facilities and wellness treatments are world-class. Regarding knives, forks, and spoons, the two dining venues, Osteria La Pergola and Restaurant Al Tramonto, have menus sprinkled with creativity and belong to the list of the best restaurants in Lake Garda. For those visiting in a romantic mood, Verona, celebrated as the city of love for its intertwined connection to Romeo and Juliet, is a 40-minute drive from Cape of Senses.

Description ⚙: The EALA My Lakeside Dream is a luxurious hotel located in Limone sul Garda, a scenic town planted in the northwestern area of Lake Garda. This 5-star adults-only hotel is known for its serene environment, installed between the sparkling waters of Lake Garda and the majestic mountains nearby. Inspired by the Celtic royal swan, the hotel's design symbolizes elegance and grace, making it a haven of tranquility and sophistication. The hotel comprises 62 rooms and suites, each offering panoramic views through expansive windows. Guests checking into the Argantos Spa Suite will have their expectations surpassed, with a private spa area, suspended bathtub, and super king size bed. Dining at this fine Lake Garda hotel is a highlight, with the SENSO Lake Garda restaurant — curated by Michelin-starred Chef Alfio Ghezzi — offering an exceptional fine-dining experience with a dining room suspended above the lake and an open kitchen. The Alfio Ghezzi Bistrot provides a more informal but equally refined alternative. The Panorama Lounge Bar, located at the hotel's highest point, offers stunning views of Lake Garda, perfect for enjoying an aperitivo. In addition, the hotel treats guests to a 1,500 m² wellness center featuring a panoramic Finnish sauna, Turkish bath, salt cabin, indoor and outdoor pools, and an array of massages and treatments. The relaxing moments continue at the hotel's private beach, a rare feature even among Lake Garda luxury hotels. Awarded two Michelin Keys by the Michelin Guide.

Summary: A neoclassical 19th-century villa at the heart of Sirmione, surrounded by five hectares of gardens that reach a private lake pier. The terrace suites on the third floor face the water directly — and the Belvedere restaurant earns its name after dark.
Description ⚙: If one looks closely at Lake Garda's map and turns it upside down, it will quickly realize its hearted shape. At the very core of this imaginary heart lies Sirmione, a lakeside town that seems to exhale romance from every angle. In such an idyllic location, one address stands out: the opulent Villa Cortine Palace Hotel, a preferred choice among couples seeking to be pampered by the finest Italian hospitality tradition. This sumptuous five-star property, adorned with towering stone columns, abundant marble, and palatial interiors, dates back to the 19th century and rests on five hectares of landscaped gardens enriched with sculptures, ponds, fountains, and multiple tree species, including handsome Mediterranean conifers. The Villa Cortine Palace Hotel accommodations are spread across a main building and a villa. The 54 tastefully decorated neoclassical rooms and suites offer a garden, a lake view, or a combination of both. The terrace suites on the third floor, boasting panoramic lake-facing balconies, are the icing on top of what is already a sweet cake. The hotel facilities include an outdoor heated pool, a 500 m² lake pier filled with sun loungers, and a tennis court. On a romantic note, having the opportunity to dine alfresco at the candle-lit Belvedere, surrounded by magical scents and blessed with a jaw-dropping combination of lake and mountain vistas, is the epitome of the dining opportunities at this prime Lake Garda hotel.

Summary: Established in 1888 and a National Heritage site, the Grand Hotel Fasano added four new lake-view suites in 2025 alongside a fully renovated AQVA SPA. Il Fagiano, awarded a Michelin star in 2024 under Chef Maurizio Bufi, is reason enough to book a table.
Description ⚙: First established in 1888, the Grand Hotel Fasano & Villa Principe is one of those hotels that carry the weight of time on its shoulders — the neoclassical building has been designated a National Heritage Site since 1989. Nonetheless, the historic establishment has struck the right balance between past and present and remains one of the best hotels in Lake Garda today. The water-facing hotel is located in a massive park that is known for the variety of its botanical species. In 2025, the hotel unveiled four new lake-view suites located in a newly built wing above the fully renovated AQVA SPA. The 86 rooms and suites offer elegant accommodation with lake views and balconies. The Executive rooms and the new 90 m² suites are our top recommendations. The Grand Hotel Fasano is also a dining destination in its own right. Among its four distinct restaurants managed by two talented chefs is the one-Michelin-star Il Fagiano, led by Executive Chef Maurizio Bufi, which offers a divine fine dining experience. It is outside, however, that patrons can sample exceptional cuisine next to a fabulous lake view at Trattoria Il Pescatore. The on-site AQVA SPA, inspired by ancient Roman baths and fully renovated in 2025, provides access to indoor and outdoor swimming pools connected by a tunnel passage, hydromassage, sauna, Turkish baths, gym, and a spa garden on the lake.
Address: Corso Giuseppe Zanardelli, 190, 25083 Gardone Riviera BS, Italy

Description ⚙: A 40-minute drive from Brescia, the lakefront Hotel Bella Riva stands out as a top option for those seeking a luxurious and undisturbed getaway on Lake Garda. Situated in the lovely Gardone Riviera town and a stone's throw from Fasano, the Hotel Bella Riva is home to a captivating 20-meter pool that provides enchanting water views, surrounded by lush gardens enriched with towering palm trees. For those who believe that small is beautiful, the boutique hotel's limited number of 23 rooms — including 4 Terrace and 2 View suites — proves to have just the right size to ensure a pleasant stay. Fortunately, all rooms offer a Lake Garda vista, except the Studio Room that faces the Parrocchia di San Faustino tower. Some rooms feature romantic water-facing balconies. Guests looking for a lake-view dining experience in Lake Garda will find no reason to leave the hotel premises: the on-site open-kitchen restaurant serves creative Italian cuisine with 360° panoramic views of the lake.

Hotel Tagline: From the candlelit terrace, water and mountains settle exactly where they should be.
Summary: We’d book the Suite Loggia for its private terrace over the lake, then spend evenings at the Maximilian restaurant — the candlelit alfresco terrace that, more than anywhere else in Gardone, puts the water and the mountains exactly where they should be.
Description ⚙: Hotel Villa del Sogno is a five-star neo-classical villa built in 1904 by German silk industrialist Maximilian Heydweiller, set on a hillside above Gardone Riviera on the western shore of Lake Garda. Operating as a hotel since 1916, it sits within 35,000 square meters of mature botanical gardens and parkland, offering panoramic views over the lake from its terrace, gardens, and select rooms and suites. The property comprises 32 rooms and suites, each individually decorated in a classical style with high ceilings, antique furnishings, and modern comforts. The Suite Loggia and Heydweiller Suite are the flagship accommodations, each with a private terrace and direct lake views. Third-floor terrace rooms offer balconies facing the water. The Maximilian restaurant terrace is the hotel's defining feature: a panoramic, candlelit alfresco setting directly overlooking Lake Garda, serving dinner alongside lake and mountain views. A poolside bar provides all-day lunch. The hotel is located within a five-minute walk of Lido '84, the two-Michelin-star restaurant of Chef Riccardo Camanini, and 20 minutes from the centre of Gardone Riviera. Ferry connections to other lakeside towns depart from the Fasano jetty, a short walk below the hotel.

Summary: A lakeside villa since 1885, set in a subtropical park with a private lido on the lake. Lake-view rooms look directly over the water from balconies and terraces — the Michelin-starred Arté al Lago, set within an art gallery by the waterfront, earns a reservation on its own.
Description ⚙: A lakeside villa operating as a hotel since 1885, originally the home of a noble Russian family. The 72 rooms and suites — including 30 suites, among them three two-bedroom suites — are set within a subtropical private park on the eastern bank of Lake Lugano; lake-view rooms have balconies, terraces, or loggia. The property includes a private lido on the lake, a clay tennis court, indoor pool, and spa. The crown jewel is the Ristorante Galleria Arté al Lago — a Michelin-starred restaurant set within an art gallery at the water's edge, led by Executive Chef Alessandro Boleso; the gallery rotates works by international artists. The hotel is part of the Swisstainable sustainable tourism initiative and a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World (SLH). A boat pier offers transfers to Monte Brè.
Address: Via Pico 9, 6900 Lugano, Switzerland
Nearest Airports: LUG · Lugano · 8 km

Summary: Perched on Collina d’Oro above Lugano, this all-suite hotel has lake panoramas from an elevation that opens the full arc of water and mountains. We’d book a Panorama or Signature Lake suite — both provide private spa access and the widest views on the hillside.
Description ⚙: An all-suite hotel perched on Collina d'Oro (Golden Hill) above Lugano, formerly the residence of a German prince. The 37 spacious suites are divided between garden-view and lake-view categories; the Panorama and Signature Lake suites occupy the property's most commanding positions and include private spa access. The elevated hillside location opens the full arc of Lake Lugano and the surrounding Alpine ranges in a single frame. The Principe Leopoldo restaurant is a member of Les Grandes Tables de Suisse and receives recognition in leading gastronomy guides. The hotel is a member of Relais & Châteaux. An outdoor pool, spa, fitness center, and piano bar with live music complete the offering. Located 2 km from Lugano's city center, with access to Piazza della Riforma and the waterfront.

Nearest Airports: LUG · Lugano · 4 km

Summary: On the shore of Lake Lugano in Morcote, 7 km from Lugano’s center — nearly every room faces the water from a private balcony. The Lago and Panorama restaurants both overlook the lake, and the lakeside pool keeps the view constant from morning to evening.
Description ⚙: A five-star resort on the shore of Lake Lugano in Vico Morcote, 7 km south of Lugano's city center. Nearly every room in the 87-room property faces the water from a private balcony; lake-view, Alps-view, and garden-view categories are available across rooms and suites. Two lakeside restaurants — Lago and Panorama — serve regional, Mediterranean, and international cuisine with the water visible from every table. A lakeside outdoor pool, indoor pool, and the Venus Wellness Center (sauna, hammam, hydromassage, fitness) complete the leisure offer. The hotel operates a regular shuttle to Lugano city center and organizes excursions to nearby Monte Generoso by scenic train. Part of the Swiss Diamond Group.

Hotel Tagline: Elevated above Lugano Paradiso, every suite balcony looks straight out over the lake to Monte San Salvatore.
Summary: Elevated above Lugano Paradiso with a straight-on view of Lake Lugano and Monte San Salvatore from every suite balcony. The Havana Deck cigar bar has become a Lugano institution for evening views over the water — a terrace that draws residents and hotel guests in equal measure.
Description ⚙: A four-star suite hotel elevated above Lugano Paradiso, within walking distance of the Lugano Paradiso train station and the Monte San Salvatore cable car. Following a thorough renovation, the hotel offers 65 rooms and suites with private balconies or terraces, most facing Lake Lugano and Monte San Salvatore directly. The Havana Deck cigar bar — a terrace with premium spirits, handmade cigars, and lake views — has developed a strong following among Lugano residents and is one of the most-visited hotel bars in the area. The hotel also operates a Mediterranean restaurant and a Japanese teppanyaki restaurant. An indoor panoramic pool, wellness area, and extensive parking are included. The San Salvatore cable car is accessible on foot.

Hotel Tagline: From 850 meters up, every balcony looks south over Lake Lugano and the Alps.
Summary: At 850 meters on one of Switzerland’s sunniest hillsides, this 1914 property looks south over Lake Lugano and the Alps from every balcony. The room to ask for is the Bella Vista suite, with a panoramic jacuzzi facing the water, inside a 2,200 m² spa complex.
Description ⚙: Founded in 1914 by Dr. Keller for its geomantic properties, Kurhaus Cademario Hotel & Spa has operated continuously as a wellness destination on one of Switzerland's sunniest hillsides. Situated at 850 meters above sea level — 25 minutes from Lugano's city center — the property delivers southward views over Lake Lugano and the Malcantone mountain ranges from virtually every room and outdoor space. The 82 rooms and suites range from standard lake-view categories to the Bella Vista suite, which comes with sunbeds and a panoramic jacuzzi on a private terrace, and the newer AQUA Suite. Access is exclusively for adults aged 16 and above. The DOT Spa covers 2,200 square meters and includes an indoor pool, outdoor pool, sauna world, ice fountains, hammam, Turkish bath, hydromassage benches, and a full treatment menu. Dining is at Radici Gourmet, a panoramic restaurant with lake-facing windows and terrace, led by Executive Chef Alessandro Ballerini.

Hotel Tagline: Fifteen private loggias face Lake Lugano directly, the Swiss Alps rising across the water.
Summary: On the Italian shore of Lake Lugano, 15 km from Lugano — 15 private suites, each with a loggia looking straight over the water toward the Swiss Alps. Worth staying for the La Musa rooftop restaurant, the adults-only spa, and a guest rating among the highest on the lake.
Description ⚙: A five-star adults-only boutique enclave of 15 suites on the Italian shore of Lake Lugano, set within the 60-acre subtropical park of the Parco San Marco resort, 15 km from Lugano's city center. All suites face the lake directly from private loggias; eight suite types range from Junior Loggia to the Luxury Loggia Master Suite, which includes a freestanding soaking tub and full-width lake terrace. The adults-only spa CEò offers sauna, steam bath, relaxation areas, and a full treatment menu, with access restricted to guests aged 16 and above. La Musa Restaurant & Rooftop Terrace serves gourmet Italian and Mediterranean cuisine at dinner with uninterrupted lake views; a private beach extends the property to the water's edge. Guests also have access to Parco San Marco's three pools and family spa. The property is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World and received a Michelin Key in 2024.
Address: Via del Ciclamino, 5, 22018 Cima CO, Italy
Nearest Airports: LUG · Lugano · 23 km

Hotel Tagline: Floor-to-ceiling glass frames Lake Lugano and the Alps from every one of the 26 rooms.
Summary: Opened in 2024 on the lakefront in Melide, 10 minutes from Lugano by train. All 26 rooms and suites face the water — the south-facing lake suites have the most generous terraces. The restaurant Le Rive serves dinner with uninterrupted views of Lake Lugano and the Alps.
Description ⚙: Opened in 2024 on the lakefront in the village of Melide, 10 km south of Lugano and 10 minutes by rail, this five-star boutique hotel is the newest property in the Swiss Diamond Group's Lake Lugano portfolio. Its contemporary architecture — clean lines, floor-to-ceiling glazing, lake-facing terraces — treats the panorama as the central design element. The 26 rooms and suites divide between lake-view and park-view categories; south-facing lake suites have the most expansive private terraces. The gourmet restaurant Le Rive serves dinner with uninterrupted lake views, drawing on regional Swiss-Italian produce. A seasonal outdoor pool, spa with sauna and steam bath, and direct access to lakeside walking paths complete the leisure offer. Melide station is a 5-minute walk; the Swissminiatur open-air attraction is nearby.

Hotel: InterContinental Lyon – Hotel Dieu, an IHG Hotel

Summary: The room to ask for is the Junior Suite Rhône River View — two levels, river-facing, with the Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourvière on the opposite bank. Le Dôme bar, set beneath a 32-metre Soufflot dome, is the city’s most theatrical place to end an evening.
Description ⚙: Housed in the Grand Hôtel-Dieu — one of the great 18th-century classified buildings on the Rhône quays, restored after 2013 — the InterContinental Lyon – Hotel Dieu has 144 rooms and suites designed by Jean-Philippe Nuel. The river-facing rooms and the Junior Suite Rhône River View look across the water toward the Part-Dieu skyline, with the Basilique Notre-Dame de Fourvière visible on the ridge. The 150 m² Presidential Suite has Rhône-facing balconies. Le Dôme bar operates beneath a 32-metre Soufflot dome and is the city's most architecturally distinctive bar. Restaurant Epona, led by chef Mathieu Charrois, serves regionally inspired cuisine along the grand façade of the Hôtel-Dieu. The hotel has held the World Travel Awards title of France's Leading Hotel five consecutive years through 2025 and earned a 2026 Michelin Key.
Address: 20 Quai Jules Courmont, 69002 Lyon, France
Nearest Airports: QNJ · Bron · 25 km; LYS · Saint-Exupéry · 38 km

Hotel Tagline: From Fourvière Hill, Lyon Cathedral and the Old Lyon rooftops spread below the terrace.
Summary: Reopened in April 2026 under Groupe Beauvallon, with renovated rooms and a new restaurant, bar, and salon de thé. The Medici Suite delivers the house’s widest view — Lyon Cathedral and the full sweep of Old Lyon rooftops visible from the terrace. The panoramic pool faces the same city.
Description ⚙: On Fourvière Hill in a 17th-century former convent, Villa Florentine has occupied the same position above Old Lyon since 1993. In October 2025 the property passed to Groupe Beauvallon and closed for renovation, reopening in April 2026 as Villa Florentine, A Beauvallon Hotel & Spa. The renovation preserved the glass-enclosed verrière that frames Lyon Cathedral and the rooftops of Old Lyon directly below, and added a new gastronomic restaurant under a new chef, a speakeasy-style bar, a salon de thé, and a ground-floor bistrot. The Medici Suite remains the house benchmark: elevated hill position with the cathedral façade and the full spread of the Presqu'île in view. The heated panoramic pool and spa, now Le Spa de la Villa Florentine, continue under the new ownership. The hotel is a Relais & Châteaux member.
Address: 25 Mnt Saint-Barthélémy, 69005 Lyon, France
Nearest Airports: QNJ · Bron · 29 km; LYS · Saint-Exupéry · 42 km

Hotel Tagline: From Fourvière Hill, the upper rooms hold both rivers and, on the clearest days, Mont Blanc.
Summary: Worth staying for the position alone — from the upper rooms and terrace, the view spans Lyon’s two rivers and, on the clearest days, reaches as far as Mont Blanc. The 100 m² apartment at the top of the property holds the broadest sightline in the house.
Description ⚙: Atop Fourvière Hill in Lyon's 5th arrondissement, Villa Maïa is a boutique five-star hotel with 27 rooms, 6 suites, and a 100 m² apartment, each designed with references to Japanese art. From the upper rooms and terrace the view spans both the Saône and the Rhône with the Presqu'île between them; on the clearest winter days, Mont Blanc appears on the eastern horizon. The hotel is a member of the Leading Hotels of the World. The gourmet restaurant serves panoramic city views alongside the menu. The spa draws on ancient Gallo-Roman bathing traditions with modern treatments. The landscaped gardens offer meditative views of Lyon's cityscape and rivers. The Basilique Notre-Dame de Fourvière and the Théâtre Gallo-Romain de Fourvière are within walking distance.
Address: 8 Rue Professeur Pierre Marion, 69005 Lyon, France

Hotel Tagline: From the pencil tower's upper floors, Lyon and the Alps unfold across every window.
Summary: Request a room on the upper floors of the Tour Part-Dieu — the Radisson Blu occupies the pencil-shaped tower’s top section, with every room opening onto a panoramic sweep of the city and the Alps. Celest Bar & Restaurant on the 32nd floor sets the same view over breakfast and dinner.
Description ⚙: The Radisson Blu Hotel, Lyon occupies the top ten floors of the 42-storey Tour Part-Dieu — nicknamed Le Crayon by locals for its tapered pencil profile — in the Part-Dieu business district. Every one of the 245 guest rooms has a panoramic city view, and the Alps are visible from the upper floors on clear days. Celest Bar & Restaurant on the 32nd floor, approximately 150 metres above ground, serves breakfast and dinner with a full-rotation panorama of Lyon and the surrounding massifs. The hotel is directly connected to the Westfield La Part-Dieu shopping centre and two minutes from the Gare de la Part-Dieu TGV station, making it the most convenient high-view property in the city for arriving and departing travellers.
Address: 129 Rue Servient, 69003 Lyon, France
Nearest Airports: QNJ · Bron · 15 km; LYS · Saint-Exupéry · 28 km

Hotel Tagline: From the eighth floor, the Rhône and Fourvière's basilica fill the same frame.
Summary: The rooms worth requesting are on the river-facing façade — upper floors across the Rhône toward Fourvière and the Massif des Bauges beyond. Les 3 Dômes, the panoramic restaurant on the eighth floor, makes the same frame available over breakfast and dinner.
Description ⚙: On the west bank of the Rhône at the southern end of the Presqu'île, the Sofitel Lyon Bellecour has 164 rooms and suites, with river-facing rooms on the north façade overlooking the Rhône toward the 6th arrondissement and the Basilique Notre-Dame de Fourvière on the ridge beyond. Les 3 Dômes restaurant occupies the eighth floor with 180-degree views across the Rhône and the city rooftops; chef Jérémy Ravier, a member of the Toques Blanches Lyonnaises, serves a regionally inspired menu listed in the MICHELIN Guide. Bar Le Melhor and the Light Bar terrace share the same panoramic floor. The spa offers Deep Nature and Biologique Recherche treatments. The hotel is four minutes on foot from Place Bellecour and 14 minutes from Vieux Lyon.
Address: 20 Quai du Dr Gailleton, 69002 Lyon, France

Description ⚙: A 5-star design resort built across south-facing terraced cliffs above Calheta Beach on Madeira's west coast. Its 243 rooms and suites are distributed over multiple levels, all oriented toward the Atlantic. The Hedonistic Suites have private outdoor jacuzzis with a direct ocean view. Three outdoor infinity pools descend from the upper terrace toward the beach, with the rooftop pool at the highest elevation delivering the widest south Atlantic view. Four restaurants, four bars, and a spa complete the offer.

Hotel Tagline: Three hectares of organic vine fall away to the north coast cliffs below.
Summary: A working quinta on a clifftop plateau in Santana, with three hectares of organic vine between the building and the north coast cliffs. The outdoor pool and restaurant terrace share the same northeast Atlantic panorama as the vineyards stretching away below.
Description ⚙: A 65-room hotel and working quinta on a clifftop plateau above Achada do Gramacho in Santana, northeast Madeira. The property occupies five hectares, of which three are planted with organic vines descending toward the north coast cliffs. Views from rooms and the outdoor pool take in the full northeast Atlantic coastline and the volcanic interior mountains. The hotel was fully renovated in 2020. The on-site restaurant serves Madeiran cuisine and wine from the estate's own cellar.

Hotel Tagline: Rooms hang directly above the lava pools, the open Atlantic beyond.
Summary: Built directly above Porto Moniz's famous natural lava pools on Madeira's northwest coast — the only hotel at this remove from Funchal with rooms facing the volcanic formations. The restaurant terrace overlooks the pools and the open Atlantic in the same sightline.
Description ⚙: A 4-star hotel in the fishing village of Porto Moniz, positioned directly above the island's famous natural lava rock swimming pools on the northwest coast. All rooms have balconies facing the Atlantic Ocean and the volcanic rock formations of the pool complex. The restaurant terrace overlooks the pools and the open sea. A rooftop solarium with jacuzzi provides elevated views north over the Atlantic. The hotel includes free access to the natural pools and a diving centre on site.

Description ⚙: 80 overwater and beach villas on Kihavah Huravalhi Island in the Baa Atoll UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, 35 minutes from Malé by seaplane. Hotel Tagline: Private terraces hang above the bay, pine forest rising behind, open Mediterranean ahead.
Summary: Hotel Formentor opened in 1929 and drew the world's most celebrated guests to its Cala Formentor beach; reopened as Four Seasons in August 2024, now with 110 rooms and suites, each on a private terrace above the bay — on a peninsula accessible only by road or by private boat from Port de Pollènça.
Description ⚙: Reopened in August 2024 as a Four Seasons property, this landmark resort on the Cap de Formentor peninsula dates to 1929, when it opened as Hotel Formentor. Set on a private estate of 486 hectares between Cala Formentor beach and a protected pine forest, the resort offers 110 rooms and suites, all with private terraces. Upper-floor rooms and Formentor Suites deliver panoramic views of the Mediterranean and the forested peninsula. The resort has four restaurants, a full-service spa, an adults-only pool, and a family pool, with direct access to the white-sand beach.

Summary: The drawbridge goes up at sunset and the Bay of Palma belongs entirely to the guests. Built into a 19th-century military fortress declared a National Monument, this adults-only hotel has 30 rooms carved from stone — each looking out over the same water that once had to be defended.
Description ⚙: Cap Rocat occupies a 19th-century military fortress on a private headland above the Bay of Palma, declared both a Heritage Asset and a National Monument. The fortress, set within a 120-hectare protected natural area, has been converted into an adults-only hotel of 30 rooms and suites, each built into the original stone walls with private patios and terraces, most with direct Mediterranean sea views. The hotel has direct sea access via a saltwater pool built on the fortress walls and a private rocky beach cove. Two restaurants serve Mediterranean cuisine; the property is a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World and closes seasonally from mid-November to March.

Description ⚙: Located on the northwest coast of Mallorca, Jumeirah Mallorca occupies a clifftop position above Port de Sóller, overlooking the natural harbor and the Serra de Tramuntana, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Eleven low-rise buildings are linked by garden walkways across 500 meters of cliff. The hotel offers 121 rooms and suites, all with private balconies or terraces oriented toward the Mediterranean or the Tramuntana range. The hotel features five restaurants and lounges, an adults-only infinity pool, a family pool, and the award-winning Talise Spa.

Summary: Deà has drawn artists and writers since Robert Graves settled there in 1929. La Residencia sits at the edge of that same village: 13 hectares of olive groves and terraced gardens on a hillside facing the Tramuntana ridge, with the Mediterranean visible in the valley below.
Description ⚙: La Residencia occupies two 16th-century manor houses on a 13-hectare hillside estate at the edge of the village of Deà, in the Serra de Tramuntana. The hotel gardens include olive trees, citrus groves, and herb gardens, with views across the valley to the mountain ridgeline and the Mediterranean beyond. Rooms and suites are furnished in traditional Mallorcan style; Executive Suites and upper-floor suites offer panoramic views of Deà and the Tramuntana, and several suites and villas have private plunge pools. Three restaurants include El Olivo in a 500-year-old olive press. The property is seasonal, open from March to November.

Description ⚙: The St. Regis Mardavall occupies a terraced clifftop position on the southwest coast of Mallorca between the Tramuntana foothills and the Mediterranean Sea. The resort consists of four terracotta-hued low-rise buildings with 125 rooms and suites, all featuring large private terraces with Mediterranean views. Butler service is standard for all guests. Description ⚙: A top Manila hotel in the Makati Central Business District, Discovery Primea is renowned for its luxurious accommodations and strategic location. Designed by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Kenzo Tange and housed in a 68-story tower — one of Manila's tallest skyscrapers — the hotel occupies the lower floors, ensuring wonderful city vistas at every level. It is a stone's throw from Greenbelt Shopping Mall, Glorietta by Ayala Malls, and Rustan's Department Store. The hotel features a heated 20-meter infinity pool with panoramic views of Manila's skyline, a 24/7 fitness center, and the Terazi Spa with traditional Turkish baths. On-site dining includes Restaurant Tapenade (Mediterranean cuisine) and Flame (contemporary continental fine dining). Rooms feature kitchenettes and floor-to-ceiling windows.

Amenities include a bay-facing infinity pool, a 24/7 Life Fitness-equipped fitness center, and a luxurious spa with captivating views. Hotel Tagline: Century-old olive trees in the foreground, the Koutoubia minaret's tile inlay sharp beyond them.
Summary: The Koutoubia Suite's windows face Marrakech's 12th-century minaret directly — the tile inlay visible at distance. Seven hectares of Moorish garden give garden-facing rooms a second view: bougainvillea, century-old olive trees, and the Atlas Mountains on clear winter mornings.
Description ⚙: Set within 7 hectares of historic gardens established in the 18th century as a royal wedding gift, La Mamounia has been Marrakech's most celebrated address since opening in 1923. Its 135 rooms and 71 suites occupy a beautifully renovated interior where Art Deco and Moroccan craftsmanship — carved cedar ceilings, zellige tilework, mashrabiya screens — intersect across every corridor. Rooms divide between garden-facing and city-facing orientations; the Koutoubia Suite and upper-floor rooms have direct sight lines to the 12th-century Koutoubia Mosque minaret, with the tile inlay and golden orb visible at close range. Below, century-old olive, orange, and rose gardens create a further layer of view available from lower-floor rooms and poolside terraces. Six restaurants and bars span Moroccan, Italian, Asian, and French cuisine.
Address: Avenue Bab Jdid، مراكش 40040, Morocco

Hotel Tagline: After dark, the illuminated Koutoubia minaret rises above medina rooftops from your private terrace.
Summary: Each of the 53 private riads at Royal Mansour climbs three floors, ending in a rooftop terrace that belongs only to your riad — no shared pool, no other guests. From up there, after dark, the illuminated Koutoubia Mosque minaret rises above the medina rooftops less than 400 meters away.
Description ⚙: The Royal Mansour, commissioned by Morocco's King Mohammed VI and completed in 2010, is built as a medina within a medina: a private compound of 53 riads, each spanning three floors, each with a private courtyard, plunge pool, and exclusive rooftop terrace. The tri-level format reaches its climax at the top: medina rooftops, date palms, and the Koutoubia Mosque minaret after dark — from a perch no other guest can access. Four restaurants and four bars serve Moroccan, Italian, Mediterranean, and international menus. Le Spa du Royal Mansour occupies three underground floors with 13 treatment rooms.

Villas with private terraces share the same orientation — breakfast to Atlas Mountains, unfiltered.
Description ⚙: The Four Seasons Resort Marrakech occupies 16 hectares of Moorish gardens between the ancient Medina and the Ville Nouvelle, oriented due south toward the High Atlas range. Its elevated main pool deck provides an unobstructed sightline toward the Atlas Mountains — the range visible year-round, snowcapped between November and April, turning purple at sunset. The 139 individually furnished rooms and suites include Pavilion Rooms with garden access, One-Bedroom Suites, and Signature Suites with private plunge pools; all upper-floor rooms have south-facing terrace or balcony access. Three restaurants serve Moroccan, Mediterranean, and poolside cuisine. A full-service spa features eight treatment rooms, hammams, and plunge pools.

Its 56 pool villas and seven suites are oriented toward the range, with private terraces framed by wooden beams overhead and the resort's pool in the foreground. Each villa has its own plunge pool. Description ⚙: Selman Marrakech, located 5 kilometers south of the city on Route d'Amizmiz, was designed around a working stud farm of purebred Barb and Arabian horses. Three outdoor pools and the outdoor restaurant terrace are oriented due south toward the High Atlas, with the horse paddocks between the hotel and the range. A Chenot spa and three restaurants — including a Spanish tapas venue at the horse stables — and two bars complete the offering.

The outdoor pool is framed by clipped hedges with the minaret rising immediately to the right. Three outdoor pools, two cocktail bars, and two restaurants are distributed across the property. El Fenn joined the AKAN Collection in November 2025.

An 18-hole golf course plays against the same backdrop on every fairway. Four outdoor pools, four restaurants, and a full-service spa complete the property.

The view from bed is Catalans Bay, framed by the Frioul Islands and the Château d'If. Every room category — from Cosy to top-floor suites with terraces of up to 45 square meters — has direct sea exposure. The hotel's restaurant, set almost at water level, serves an inventive Mediterranean cuisine with Asian influences. A mineral spa carved into the Corniche rock houses a hammam, sauna, and heated indoor pool. A second-floor rooftop terrace is open to outside guests; a fifth-floor heated infinity pool is reserved for hotel residents. Green Key certified and listed in the Michelin Guide hotel selection. Adjacent to Plage des Catalans and five minutes' walk from the Vieux Port.

Description ⚙: The InterContinental Marseille - Hotel Dieu expertly blends historic grandeur with modern luxury in Marseille's oldest neighbourhood, Le Panier. The 194 rooms and suites include units facing the Old Port and the basilica, with a number extending to private terraces. The Presidential Suite is the property's most impressive accommodation; the Junior Suite Terrace category delivers additional space and a captivating view. Les Fenêtres brasserie serves breakfast and lunch with views of Notre-Dame de la Garde. The Capian Bar offers a curated cocktail menu. The SPA by Clarins provides a full range of treatments and an indoor pool, and the fitness centre is open 24 hours.

Description ⚙: Le Petit Nice - Passedat has graced the Marseille coastline since 1917. A Relais & Châteaux member, this family-owned boutique property has no more than 16 guest rooms and suites, each designed to merge comfort with the minimalist elegance of Mediterranean life. All rooms offer panoramic sea views of the Frioul Islands and the Mediterranean beyond. The décor, by architect Rudy Ricciotti, uses high-quality materials that enhance natural light and the coastal vistas. The property is especially renowned for its three-Michelin-star restaurant, led by Chef Gérald Passedat, whose seafood-forward menus highlight local Mediterranean catch and are enjoyed with direct sea views. The hotel also offers a seaside garden, terrace, and heated outdoor seawater pool. Complimentary minibars and refined bath products are standard across all rooms and suites.

The 134 rooms and suites are elegantly decorated with maritime themes. Many rooms offer views of the Old Port, with select suites featuring private terraces or balconies. The Prestige and Opera suites provide expansive top-floor views with private lounges. The hotel operates three panoramic venues: the Dantès Skylounge, a 150-square-meter cocktail terrace on the top floor with views from the MUCEM to Notre-Dame de la Garde; Les Trois Forts, a gastronomic restaurant led by Chef Sylvain Touati; and Le Carré Bistromanie, a brasserie with a port-facing terrace. Description ⚙: The Four Seasons Hotel at The Surf Club occupies a singular address at 9011 Collins Avenue in Surfside: the site of the former Surf Club, a private beach establishment founded in 1930 that counted Rockefeller, Churchill, and much of the twentieth century's social register among its members. The complex opened in 2017 as a Four Seasons property, combining the painstakingly restored historic building — its barrel-vaulted ceilings, coral stone columns, and garden courtyard intact — with a contemporary oceanfront tower designed by Richard Meier. The tower's Premier Ocean View and One-Bedroom Ocean View Suite categories look directly onto the Atlantic; upper floors deliver unobstructed sightlines extending north toward Bal Harbour and south toward the South Beach skyline. Dining at The Surf Club is among the primary reasons to book the property. The Surf Club Restaurant, overseen by Thomas Keller, maintains the precision and sourcing standards associated with his flagship kitchens, translated into an oceanside setting. The spa spans 36,000 square feet across multiple treatment wings, with an indoor pool and full wellness programming.

The Art Deco-era pool at beach level puts the Atlantic in constant frame; the Oceanfront Balcony Penthouse extends the panorama in both directions along the coast. Chef Abram Bissell’s Pauline is the dining draw.
Description ⚙: The Shelborne opened in 1940 at 1801 Collins Avenue, designed by Igor Polevitzky with later contributions from Morris Lapidus, who added the pool pavilion and cabanas that remain the most photographed elements of the property today. Proper Hotels acquired the site and commissioned a $100 million renovation with design studio ADC & Tuneu. The result reopened in May 2025 as The Shelborne By Proper. The renovation restored the two-story lobby windows that Lapidus had designed but which had been obscured for decades, flooding the ground floor with the natural light the original scheme intended. The 251 guest rooms and suites were fully rethought, with oceanfront categories now offering private balconies and direct Atlantic views. The top-floor Oceanfront Balcony Penthouse extends the panorama north and south along the coastline. The Art Deco-era pool at beach level remains the architectural centrepiece of the property: its position directly on the sand makes the Atlantic an immediate presence rather than a backdrop. Chef Abram Bissell leads the kitchen at Pauline, the hotel's signature restaurant, where a locally driven menu is served in a room that opens to a garden terrace.
Address: 1801 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL 33139, USA

Hotel Tagline: From the 40th floor, a private infinity pool meets the Atlantic's blue and turquoise panorama.
Summary: The forty-story Setai tower has held its position on Collins Avenue since 2005. Ocean Suites on the upper floors deliver the widest Atlantic panorama on the strip; the 40th-floor penthouse adds a private infinity pool to that view. Three temperature-varied pools and the Valmont Spa make the case for staying in entirely.
Description ⚙: When it opened in 2005, the forty-story Setai tower triumphantly took its place on Miami Beach's sands to become a premier destination in South Beach. Known for its dark wood decor, Asian-inspired serenity, and top-of-the-line amenities, The Setai, Miami Beach offers luxury at a price. The spacious rooms are furnished with Dux mattresses, and some boast sunken tubs. From the 140 accommodations, the Ocean Suites are a natural option for those looking to admire Miami's coastline from the privacy of their quarters. The 10,000-square-foot penthouse occupies the 40th floor and features lavish additions like a Steinway grand piano, two jacuzzis, and a private infinity pool; views offer a beautiful panorama of blue and turquoise ocean waters and Miami's downtown skyline in the distance. Dining options are a highlight, with restaurants like the Asian-inspired Jaya offering exquisite meals. Alternatively, the beachfront Ocean Grill restaurant is ideal for a more laid-back meal. The Setai, Miami Beach, offers a serene oasis with three temperature-varied pools. The Valmont Spa provides facials, massages, and a range of services that exclusively utilize Valmont spa and skincare products.

Summary: The eco-committed 1 Hotel rises from the Roney Palace site in Mid-Beach. Ocean View and Oceanfront suites command balcony views directly over the Atlantic. The rooftop pool and alfresco dining add elevation to the same panorama — worth staying for the beach access alone, across three pools including one oceanfront.
Description ⚙: The oceanfront 1 Hotel South Beach, envisioned by hotelier Barry Sternlicht, stands as a beacon of luxury and sustainability in Miami. It offers guests an eco-friendly oasis with a distinct emphasis on natural materials and environmental consciousness — in-hotel dry cleaning, hemp-blended Keetsa mattresses, natural cleansers, and reclaimed wood walls from Colorado beetle-killed pine. The upscale Ocean View and Oceanfront suites, featuring a scenic balcony facing the beach and the ocean, elevate this property to one of the best hotels in Miami on Collins Avenue. This is the third hotel to occupy the space within the large Roney Palace condo building, following the Gansevoort and its successor, the Perry. The 1 Hotel South Beach's top-notch amenities include two beautiful pools, a state-of-the-art gym, and multiple dining options, including superb gluten-free choices. The rooftop offers breathtaking ocean views and is a perfect spot for alfresco dining, while the beach level provides a more laid-back atmosphere with freshly grilled foods.

Hotel Tagline: Oversized windows frame the Atlantic Ocean or the Miami skyline from 171 rooms on Collins Avenue.
Summary: Ian Schrager’s legendary Art Deco address on Collins Avenue reopened in March 2026 after a six-year renovation by Ennismore. The 171 rooms and Poolside Bungalow Suites frame the Atlantic or the Miami skyline; the revival of the Rose Bar and Paris Society’s first U.S. restaurant anchor the most anticipated return in South Beach’s recent history.
Description ⚙: The original Delano opened on Collins Avenue in 1947; the version that defined South Beach's cultural moment arrived in the 1990s under hotelier Ian Schrager and designer Philippe Starck, whose white-on-white interiors, floor-to-ceiling curtains, and the legendary Rose Bar effectively inaugurated the modern era of lifestyle hospitality in the United States. The hotel closed in March 2020 for what became a comprehensive six-year renovation by Elastic Architects, in partnership with Ennismore and Cain International. It reopened on March 9, 2026. The 171 rooms and suites — including Poolside Bungalow Suites and Penthouse Suites — maintain the Delano's signature tonal palette: organic fluidity, bespoke lighting, and oversized windows that frame either the Atlantic Ocean or the Miami skyline. Two pools anchor the property: the original ground-level pool, now joined by a second pool on the fourth floor with a new beachfront amenity deck. Four food and beverage concepts accompany the reopening, including the revival of the Rose Bar, Gigi Rigolatto (Paris Society's first American outpost), and Mimi Kakushi.

Every room faces the Atlantic from a glass-walled balcony; upper floors deliver unobstructed sightlines from Bal Harbour to Fort Lauderdale. Description ⚙: The Ritz-Carlton Bal Harbour occupies the northernmost point of the Collins Avenue luxury corridor at 10295 Collins Avenue — a deliberate distance from South Beach that serves guests who come specifically for the quieter stretch of beach, the proximity to Bal Harbour Shops, and the sense of seclusion that the area's lower density provides. The hotel's oceanfront position means every room category is oriented toward the Atlantic, with glass-walled balconies extending the interior space onto the water's edge. The tower's upper floors deliver sightlines that extend north toward Fort Lauderdale and south along the curve of the Miami Beach coastline. Ocean View and Ocean View Suite categories add private dining areas and expanded terrace space to the standard balcony panorama. The Exhale Spa operates as a distinguishing element of the property, offering a wellness programme that goes beyond standard hotel spa services to include fitness classes, energy work, and integrated recovery treatments. The private beach and beach club are managed with a service ratio that matches the room inventory.

We’d book the Royal Ocean View Suite for its panoramic windows over Lummus Park and the beach. The rooftop pool adds altitude to the Atlantic view; Laurent Tourondel’s LT Steak & Seafood handles dinner below.
Description ⚙: The Betsy Hotel, South Beach, is steps away from Miami Beach Ocean Walk and stands out as an elegant contrast to the surrounding Art Deco architecture. Known for its stately Southern charm, the hotel underwent a comprehensive renovation in 2006. The redesign features a sophisticated Christian Liaigre palette with dark walnut floors complemented by rich red, green, lilac, and ochre accents. The hotel is a cultural hub featuring live piano music daily, and a poetry bridge. For those seeking the pinnacle of luxury and comfort, the Royal Ocean View Suite at this oceanfront hotel is a must. This suite features expansive windows offering breathtaking views of Ocean Drive, Lummus Park, and the beach. Each morning, guests can start their day with breakfast on the deck overlooking Ocean Drive, appreciating the direct ocean views and easy access to the beach with provided sunbeds and umbrellas. Heading to the hotel's rooftop pool with captivating Atlantic vistas will undoubtedly be one of the highlights of this Miami stay. A notable highlight of The Betsy Hotel, South Beach, is the inclusion of Laurent Tourondel's LT Steak & Seafood, celebrated for its unique approach to cuisine, appealing to a discerning clientele.

The Oceanfront Balcony Room is the address for a majestic sunrise. The Matador Room, led by Jean-Georges Vongerichten, is one of the few hotel restaurants in Miami worth booking on its own terms.
Description ⚙: Ian Schrager, co-founder of the celebrated Studio 54, pioneered the American boutique hotel concept. The Miami Beach EDITION, nestled in an area with spacious vintage hotels from the 1950s, offers a prime beachfront location that combines luxury, impeccable service, and exceptional amenities. Guests are welcomed into a world of minimalist elegance featuring a serene interior design of white and light wood finishes, accentuated by lush greenery. The hotel is celebrated for its spacious rooms, with large baths enhancing the experience. Guests enjoy stunning views from the Oceanfront Balcony Room, perfect for a majestic sunrise. The Premiere Bungalow Ocean View Suite category features a plunge pool, rainforest shower, and Le Labo amenities for those looking for truly luxurious oceanfront accommodations. This Collins Avenue hotel features the Basement disco and various recreational activities, including a pool table, bowling alley, and ice-skating rink. A talented chef oversees the culinary delights; the Matador Room signature restaurant by Jean-Georges Vongerichten and the on-site bars provide outstanding dining experiences. Guests can also relax at multiple pools and a spa equipped with a hammam, sauna, and treatment rooms.

Hotel Tagline: From the wraparound balcony of the corner suite, the Atlantic fills every angle.
Summary: The Saxony Hotel’s bones survive inside Alan Faena’s extravagant reimagining — Baz Luhrmann and Catherine Martin’s interiors, gold pillars, a Damien Hirst mammoth by the pool. The Premier Oceanfront Corner Suite wraps a wraparound ocean panorama around a private balcony; Francis Mallmann’s Los Fuegos delivers the open-fire asado dinner.
Description ⚙: Argentine hotelier Alan Faena transformed the historic Saxony Hotel into a lavish destination. The reimagined Faena Hotel Miami Beach retains the original terrazzo floors but introduces an extravagant interior combining the charm of the 1950s and Miami's beloved Art Deco architecture. The lobby boasts gold pillars and striking murals by Juan Gotti. The 58 guest rooms and 121 suites, designed by filmmakers Baz Luhrmann and Catherine Martin, feature a rich palette of gold, blue, and red. Those lodging in the Premier Oceanfront Corner Suite can expect an upgraded stay with sweeping ocean vistas enjoyed from a wraparound, expansive panoramic balcony. Artistic opulence continues throughout the hotel, notably with a Damien Hirst piece — a gold-coated mammoth skeleton encased in hurricane-proof glass — displayed near the pool. The property's location right on the beach provides easy access to South Beach. Guests are invited to unwind on the private beach, embark on a holistic experience at Tierra Santa Healing House, and dine at the excellent live-cooking restaurant Los Fuegos by Francis Mallmann, known for its signature asados. Entertainment is part of Faena Hotel Miami Beach's DNA, highlighted by a two-story cabaret theatre.

Summary: The 2009 property that shifted the centre of gravity northward on Collins Avenue. Every room has a private balcony with ocean views — a consistency the W holds over most of its neighbours. The Extreme WOW Suite adds an outdoor plunge pool to that Atlantic panorama. We’d use the evenings at Wall and Mr. Chow, and the AWAY Spa for recovery.
Description ⚙: When it opened in 2009, the beachfront W South Beach dramatically shifted the Miami social and nightlife scene. This trendsetting hotel, sitting next to Collins Park, features a Mr. Chow Chinese restaurant right on Collins Avenue, a Living Room bar adjacent to a conceptual garden designed by Paula Hayes, an AWAY spa, and an ultralounge named Wall, all housed in a modern nineteen-story building by architect Costas Kondylis. The W South Beach influence is magnified by its connection to Aby Rosen, a renowned New York art collector who enhances the hotel's decor with museum-quality art pieces. Epitomizing Miami's persona, the Extreme WOW Suite boasts an outdoor plunge pool, a Japanese soaking tub, and an expansive, luxurious space with ocean views. In addition, the hotel boasts spacious and elegantly furnished rooms with breathtaking ocean views, modern furniture, and convenient kitchenettes. Every room has a private balcony with ocean views. The late architect Zaha Hadid chose the W South Beach as her Miami residence, merging two units to create her space.

South-facing rooms claim a broader panorama; north-facing rooms take in the full beach expanse. Description ⚙: The beachfront, hyper-luxurious The St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort, opened in 2012, replaced the nostalgic 1956 Americana hotel with a modern twenty-seven-storey tower where every room boasts an ocean view. The architectural design leaves the front facade unadorned, except for a cantilevered portico that marks a discreet entrance. Upon entering the mirrored lobby, guests are greeted with a warm welcome. The interior, designed by Toronto-based Yabu Pushelberg, melds modern glamour with elements like chandeliers and marble, balancing luxury with minimalism. Each room extends into a glass-walled balcony, offering expansive views. The St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort is not just a luxurious oceanfront retreat but a gateway to a world of culinary and retail delights. Located just steps away from top-notch restaurants and shopping, with the Bal Harbour Shops mall directly across the street. The hotel boasts multiple dining options, including the Greek-inspired restaurant Atlantikos, serving a breakfast buffet and a menu featuring salads, skewers, and grilled Atlantic-sourced fish.

Description ⚙: Located where the lively Lincoln Road intersects with Collins Avenue, the oceanfront Loews Miami Beach Hotel is near many dining and nightlife options along the South Beach area, including the renowned Espanola Way Street. Steeped in history, the Loews Miami Beach Hotel was established in 1998, marking a significant milestone for Miami Beach. Nestled in one of Miami's most pictured Art Deco buildings, the hotel, renovated in 2010, is a fine example of Miami's rich architectural heritage. The 790 rooms and suites stand out for their cleanliness, comfort, and breathtaking ocean views. Many feature balconies that provide scenic vistas of the pool and the ocean. If the ocean vistas are the ultimate prize, the sight of Miami's skyline to the west is also impressive. The pool area is optimally sized, complete with plentiful beach chairs and a pool bar that offers convenient snack and drink service. The beach service further enriches guest stays.

Description ⚙: Positioned between the Faena Hotel and The Miami Beach EDITION at 3025 Collins Avenue, The Palms Hotel & Spa occupies a quieter register than its high-profile neighbours while sharing the same direct access to the Atlantic. The hotel's most distinctive physical feature is its grounds: a tropical garden planted with baobab trees, palms, and flowering species that create a layered courtyard between the street and the beach. The result is an atmosphere closer to a boutique resort than the social hotels that bracket it on either side. The oceanfront rooms and suites face the Atlantic directly from private balconies. The oceanfront pool faces the water, and beach service is provided with chairs, towels, and food and beverage attention. The Palms Spa offers a full treatment menu. Elements Restaurant handles dining across breakfast, lunch, and dinner; the outdoor terrace, set within the baobab garden, provides an alternative to the pool and beach settings.

The Martini Room and retro Marshall speakers calibrate the experience at a pace the neighbouring hotels don’t attempt. The adjacent Delano, which reopened in March 2026, has restored the block.
Description ⚙: The National Hotel, a grand structure from 1939, holds a prime spot between the reimagined Delano — which reopened in March 2026 after a six-year renovation — and the art-centric Sagamore. While neighboring hotels underwent significant transformations, the National Hotel maintained its original charm, especially after Delphine Dray's $10 million investment in a renovation effort that enhanced the hotel while respecting its historical roots. The National Hotel's refurbishment has beautifully preserved its classic elegance, updating the classy lobby with club chairs and period lighting, restoring the Martini Room, and maintaining its status as having the longest pool in Miami Beach. Modern amenities like flat-screen TVs, seamlessly blending into the decor, ensure a comfortable and luxurious stay. The retro Marshall sound speakers are a wonderful addition. The hotel boasts impressive facilities, including two tranquil pools and a stylish bar. Guests can enjoy direct beach access with complimentary beach chairs — a rarity in South Beach.

The spa offers eleven treatment rooms with ocean orientation.
Description ⚙: A quintessentially luxurious Miami experience, The Ritz-Carlton, South Beach, located at the iconic address of 1 Lincoln Road in Miami Beach, is a five-star oceanfront hotel that combines the glamour of Miami's Art Deco heritage with modern-day amenities. Designed by legendary architect Morris Lapidus and opened as The DiLido Hotel in 1953. The hotel offers several room categories, including those with much sought-after stunning views of the ocean. Notable among these are the Club Oceanfront Suite, the Lanai Oceanfront Suite, and The Ritz-Carlton Suite. Standard to all rooms and suites are premium perks such as marble bathrooms, double vanities, and La Bottega Diptyque amenities. Guests are invited to enjoy diverse facilities: a top-notch spa with eleven treatment rooms, a state-of-the-art fitness center, and a landscaped outdoor pool that overlooks the Atlantic Ocean. Dining options include the DiLido Beach Bar, which offers al fresco, oceanfront meals, and Zaytinya by Jose Andres Group, which offers a menu that draws inspiration from Turkish, Greek, and Lebanese flavors.

The hotel was initially celebrated for its stylish interiors designed by Parisian talent Jacques Garcia, known for his work on the Hotel Costes. Despite its lively surroundings, the hotel ensures a peaceful retreat with soundproofing that keeps the bustling street noise at bay. For those looking for the best accommodation in the house, getting hold of the Victoria Penthouse is a must; featuring a private plunge pool and an oceanfront terrace facing Miami Beach, it really doesn't get any better than this. The design follows the Andaz approach: an open lobby that doubles as a social gathering space, locally commissioned art, and room categories that prioritise floor space and natural light. It is close to Collins Park and the acclaimed Bass Art Museum. While Morris Lapidus is credited with the interior work, including the restaurant and possibly the porte cochere, the structure itself was the brainchild of architects Melvin Grossman and Albert Anis. After years of being under the radar, the renovated Nautilus Sonesta Miami Beach now garners accolades for its amenities. Guests enjoy the salt-water pool, stylish lobby, beachfront loungers, cool interior decor, and attentive service. The rooms offer comfort and style, but for the full experience, a room or suite with a terrace and ocean view is highly recommended; for instance, the King Balcony Oceanfront features floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows and a picture-perfect balcony to enjoy the Atlantic's breeze.

Description ⚙: Adjacent to the Alter Botanischer Garten in Maxvorstadt, the hotel was built in 2007 as part of the regeneration of its neighbourhood. Many rooms have French balconies with garden views, and the Royal Suite Montforte on the top floor has a panoramic sundeck facing Old Town and the Frauenkirche. The garden-facing Florio restaurant serves Italian cuisine with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the park.

Description ⚙: Opened in June 2024, the Koenigshof marks The Luxury Collection's debut in Germany and the first significant new-build luxury hotel at Karlsplatz in decades. Designed by architects Nieto Sobejano Arquitectos, the building occupies a historic address at the centre of Munich. The Panorama Suites face Karlsplatz with the Frauenkirche visible above the roofline; the private spa pool on the upper floors overlooks Munich's rooftops with the Alps visible on clear days. GRETA OTO restaurant is located on the ninth floor with city panoramas.
