Description ⚙: A designated public monument, The Fullerton Hotel Singapore occupies a majestic 1920s neo-classical building that once housed the General Post Office and Library. Since opening as a hotel on January 1, 2001, it has established itself as a landmark Marina Bay address. Eight Loft Suites with the signature of Aston Design were unveiled in 2022, each featuring spiral staircases and private balconies flanked by Doric columns with direct views of Marina Bay Sands. The Town Restaurant commands panoramic views over Marina Bay and Raffles Place and hosts one of Singapore's most celebrated Sunday brunches.

Description ⚙: Designed by Pritzker laureate Kevin Roche and opened in 1996, The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore occupies three hectares of gardens on the Marina Bay waterfront. The 32-story glass-and-steel hotel is distinguished by its octagonal bathroom windows positioned along exterior walls, framing Marina Bay, Raffles Place, Kallang River, or island views from the bathtub. High-floor Premier Suites ending in 26 command the widest bay panoramas. The hotel holds a 4,200-piece collection of art including works by Frank Stella and Dale Chihuly. Dining includes the Colony Sunday brunch and Summer Pavilion for Cantonese cuisine. La Mer spa features treatments accompanied by live music.

Description ⚙: Swissôtel The Stamford Singapore opened in 1986 as the world's tallest hotel at the time and continues to offer some of Singapore's most expansive panoramic views. The 70th floor houses both the SKAI bar and JAAN by Kirk Westaway, a two-Michelin-star restaurant with 35 seats and a 360-degree skyline backdrop. On clear days, Indonesian and Malaysian islands are visible from the upper floors. Over a thousand rooms feature Marina Bay and Singapore skyline views from private balconies, with the Marina Bay Sands towers visible from reserved rooms. The hotel sits directly above City Hall MRT and connects to Raffles City Shopping Centre.

Description ⚙: The Pan Pacific Singapore, designed by John Portman, features a dramatic 35-floor internal ziggurat atrium rising above Marina Square. A $30 million renovation completed in 2023 refreshed the lobby, driveway, and over 500 rooms while preserving the hotel's iconic architectural elements. The Skyline Suites on upper floors deliver the property's finest Marina Bay panoramas. The Pacific Club Lounge on the 38th floor is accessible via a 38-second express elevator and offers city vistas alongside full club amenities. The Japanese restaurant Keyaki occupies a garden setting on the property grounds.

Marina Bay hotel suites frame MBS and the Esplanade in the same window. Flow18 Sky Garden for events.
Description ⚙: The JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach opened in 2015 as part of a mixed-use development masterminded by Lord Norman Foster. The complex integrates offices, residences, retail, and the 634-room hotel in a prime location between the convention centre and Raffles Singapore. The 18th floor serves as the hotel's recreational crown, with a panoramic pool deck, fitness centre, and Singapore skyline views. Marina Bay hotel suites frame Marina Bay Sands and the Esplanade. The Flow18 Sky Garden and Ebb6 Sky Garden provide alfresco event spaces with city panoramas. Dining extends across The NCO Club, a heritage building serving multiple themed restaurants.

Description ⚙: The Palácio de Seteais has operated as a hotel since 1954, and since January 2024 under the Valverde Group — a 30-year concession from the Portuguese State — as the Valverde Sintra Palácio de Seteais, a member of The Leading Hotels of the World. All 30 rooms and suites face the Sintra Mountains; the Royal Suite captures both the Moorish Castle and Pena Palace from the same balcony. Restaurante Seteais serves Portuguese and international cuisine in a frescoed ballroom, and the spa is set between the manicured gardens.

Description ⚙: The only hotel inside the Sintra-Cascais Natural Park, set within the grounds of a 14th-century monastery. Rooms and suites face the golf course or the Sintra Mountains; the Cascais, Sintra, and Imperial suites add oversized terraces. Description ⚙: Time slows down along the Riva degli Schiavoni, where Londra Palace Venezia presides over one of Venice's most coveted viewpoints. Savvy travelers linger at their balconies here, watching gondolas glide past against the backdrop of San Giorgio Maggiore island, while the dome of Santa Maria delle Salute Church punctuates the western horizon. The hotel's position, just moments from St. Mark's Square and the Doge's Palace, places guests at the crossroads of Venice's grandeur, with St. Zacharias' Church beckoning around the corner. Behind the historic façade of this 19th-century merger between the Angleterre and Beau Rivage hotels, 52 rooms and suites unfold like chapters in a Venetian novel. Each space tells its own tale through thoughtfully curated elements — tapestries dance at windows, brocade embraces walls, and authentic Biedermeier furniture grounds the historical narrative. Some guests swear the lagoon views are most magical from the balconies and loggias, where purple, grey, or ivory color schemes create serene retreats from Venice's bustle. The top-floor rooms reveal their age proudly through exposed wooden beams, while pink Carrara marble bathrooms catch the perfume of lagoon breezes through generous windows. LPV Ristorante at Londra Palace Venezia orchestrates a culinary journey through Venice's rich gastronomic heritage. Throughout the day, LondraBar's veranda becomes a front-row seat to the theater of Venetian life unfolding along the Riva. Those in the know whisper about the rooftop altana terrace, where intimate gatherings of up to eight guests can dine under the stars, surrounded by Venice's illuminated spires. The hotel reopened in March 2024 following an extensive renovation by Studio Ruberti Cutillo, refreshing the lobby, restaurant-bar, and terrace while preserving the soul of this historic haven.

Description ⚙: Morning light dances across the Grand Canal, where The St. Regis Venice claims Venice's most impressive waterfront. Since its 2019 metamorphosis from the historic Grand Hotel Britannia of 1895, this architectural masterpiece frames postcard-perfect views — the Santa Maria della Salute Basilica rising majestically across the water, contemporary art finding harbor at Punta della Dogana Museum, and San Giorgio Maggiore's bell tower piercing the horizon. In the 163 guestrooms and suites, Sagrada design studio's vision captures Venice's legendary light through contemporary eyes. Some fortunate guests wake to Grand Canal panoramas from private terraces, while others overlook the hotel's secret Italianate garden or Venice's timeless terracotta roofscape. The Monet Suites tell their artistic tale — their color palettes echo the same views that inspired the master's brush during his Venetian sojourns. Chef Giuseppe Ricci orchestrates culinary theater at Gio's Restaurant & Terrace, where innovative Italian cuisine meets Grand Canal drama. The Arts Bar writes its contemporary narrative through cocktails that pay tribute to provocateurs like Jeff Koons and Banksy. Art flows through The St. Regis Venice like another canal — Ai Weiwei's White Chandelier commands the lobby's heights. Through its artist-in-residence program, the hotel keeps company with creativity just as it did when J.M.W. Turner and John Singer Sargent found inspiration within these walls. The hotel holds Green Key certification and operates Venice's first electric boat charging station.

Description ⚙: From its commanding position on the Grand Canal, The Gritti Palace, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Venice whispers stories of five centuries of Venetian grandeur. The 15th-century Gothic palazzo, refreshed by an artful 2013 restoration, presents a theater of Venice's most enchanting views — the dome of Santa Maria della Salute Basilica rising like a dream across the water, gondolas gliding past in graceful procession, and the vibrant waterfront life unfolding just minutes from St. Mark's Square and Teatro La Fenice. The 82 rooms and suites read like chapters from Venice's golden age. Those who secure the coveted Landmark Grand Canal rooms wake to vistas stretching from the Salute's magnificent dome to the avant-garde treasures of the Peggy Guggenheim Collection. Literary souls gravitate to the Hemingway Suite, where floor-to-ceiling French doors open to balconies suspended over the Grand Canal. Culinary artistry takes center stage at Club del Doge Restaurant, where authentic Venetian cuisine pairs with Grand Canal panoramas. The Gritti Terrace captures Venice's most sought-after sunsets, while Bar Longhi enchants with its hand-sculpted mirrors. Since 1975, the hotel has shared its culinary secrets through the Gritti Epicurean School — the world's first palace hotel cooking school — today led by Executive Chef Alberto Fol. The Gritti SPA is branded by Sisley Paris.

Description ⚙: Just a whisper away from St. Mark's Square, Baglioni Hotel Luna is a testament to Venice's enduring romance. Where Knights Hospitaller once found refuge in 1118, today's guests discover a palazzo where history seeps through every stone while lagoon views stretch to San Giorgio Island's distant silhouette. Within the 91 rooms and suites, Venetian craftsmanship takes center stage. Silk-draped walls catch the light from Murano glass chandeliers, while Italian marble bathrooms provide spaces of gleaming sanctuary. Those who secure the San Giorgio Terrace Suite find themselves with a private theater box overlooking the lagoon's daily performance. Among the most distinguished suites is the Tiziano Lagoon View Suite, offering panoramic water views. The Marco Polo Ballroom transforms breakfast into a museum visit, where 18th-century frescoes by Tiepolo's pupils float overhead like painted clouds. In the acclaimed Canova Restaurant by Sadler, Michelin-starred chef Claudio Sadler's menus are realized by resident chef Gennaro Balice. Luna Bistro caters to more casual moments, while Caffè Baglioni faces the lagoon. A refresh by The One Atelier modernized the lobby, restaurant, and bar. The hotel dates to the 12th century and is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.

Description ⚙: Venice reveals its most intimate face at Hotel Cipriani, A Belmond Hotel, Venice, where the easternmost tip of Giudecca Island cradles one of the city's most storied retreats. Early risers gathering at the wooden deck of Cip's Club swear the morning light here transforms the lagoon into liquid gold, with St. Mark's Square and the Doge's Palace emerging from the morning mist like a Renaissance painting come to life. A private launch whisks guests across to San Marco in four minutes. The 94 rooms and suites split between the main Cipriani building and Palazzo Vendramin, each offering their interpretation of Venetian grandeur. Those in the know request the Premium St. Mark's View rooms in Palazzo Vendramin; the Palladio Suite adds a 180-degree water view and private heated plunge pool. Michelin-starred Oro Restaurant is led by Chef Vania Ghedini with Massimo Bottura as culinary creative director. Cip's Club offers lagoon-side dining overlooking St. Mark's Square; Il Porticciolo serves poolside; Bar Gabbiano honors tradition with Bellinis following Giuseppe Cipriani's original 1948 recipe. The grounds feature the only Olympic-sized seawater pool in Venice, maintained at 29°C year-round, and the Casanova Gardens. In 2025, architect Peter Marino oversaw a reimagined interior covering the lobby and 13 guestrooms.

Description ⚙: On the storied Riva degli Schiavoni, Danieli, A Four Seasons Hotel, Venice rises among the city's grandest canal-view hotels. Three interconnected palaces form this Gothic masterpiece — the 15th-century Palazzo Dandolo, the 19th-century Palazzo Casa Nuova, and Palazzo Danieli Excelsior (1950) — just steps from St. Mark's Square and the Bridge of Sighs. The hotel is reopening in 2026 following a USD 34 million restoration by French interior designer Pierre-Yves Rochon, who preserved the four-storey atrium with pink marble columns and the gilded staircase while introducing Murano glass chandeliers, terrazzo floors, and a palette of soft pinks, lagoon blues, and warm terracottas. Opening with 120 rooms and suites, expanding to 176 by 2027. Lagoon-facing rooms look out across the Venetian Lagoon to San Giorgio Maggiore. Terrazza Danieli, the rooftop restaurant led by Executive Chef Adriano Rausa, offers panoramic views over the lagoon and the dome-studded skyline. Bar Dandolo, off the lobby in the original Palazzo Dandolo, provides coffee, tea, and cocktails. The Danieli Spa opens late 2026 with three treatment rooms and a sauna and hammam. General Manager Christian Zandonella leads the team for the property's new chapter under Four Seasons.

Description ⚙: Pink and proud against Venice's Grand Canal, Ca' Sagredo Hotel rises opposite the bustling Rialto Market in a display of 15th-century splendor. This Italian National Monument, once home to the influential Sagredo family, safeguards an extraordinary collection of artwork exactly where it was placed centuries ago. The palazzo's 42 rooms and suites feel less like hotel accommodations and more like chambers in a private museum. Those lucky enough to secure a Grand Canal Double room wake to the gentle splash of gondolas below their windows. Some rooms overlooking the inner courtyard offer private terraces. Book lovers gravitate to the Library Suite — once a sanctuary where Galileo himself pondered the mysteries of the universe among 10,000 volumes. The dramatic marble staircase, Andrea Tirali's 1734 masterpiece, leads to a portego grand central hall. Breakfast is served in two remarkable settings: the Sala del Doge, with a Sagredo family tree in golden leaves spanning three centuries, and the Sala del Tiepolo, crowned by one of Giambattista Tiepolo's heavenly frescoes. L'Alcova Restaurant's wooden terrace hovers just above the Grand Canal's waters. As evening falls, regulars head to the rooftop terrace with Murano glass flowers while gondolas slip silently below. A traghetto gondola ferry at the doorstep offers quick passage to the Rialto Market.

Description ⚙: Hotel Rialto occupies the Riva del Vin on the Grand Canal, directly facing the Rialto Bridge — one of the most cinematically specific positions in Venice. The four-star property has 79 individually furnished rooms and suites, 28 of which overlook the Grand Canal with direct sightlines to the bridge's white Istrian stone arch. The interiors blend traditional Venetian and contemporary styles. The recommended categories for view are the Double Classic with Grand Canal view, with the Rialto Bridge framed directly in the window, and the Honeymoon Junior Suite, which adds a private balcony over the canal. A Deluxe Apartment with a separate entrance is also available for canal-view stays. The rooftop terrace restaurant and bar offers an unobstructed view of the bridge and the canal traffic below. From April through October, breakfast is served on the ground-floor terrace with the bridge as a direct backdrop. The vaporetto stop for lines 1 and 2 is directly outside the hotel door. St. Mark's Square is a five-minute walk via the Mercerie; the Rialto Market is immediately across the bridge.

The Exclusive lagoon-view damasco suite frames the water without interruption. Vivaldi’s former chapel is now the Oriental Bar & Bistrot.
Description ⚙: Along Venice's historic Riva degli Schiavoni, Hotel Metropole Venezia claims its place among the city's most distinctive luxury hotels. What began as a humble convent and orphanage now enchants visitors with its prime position between Piazza San Marco and the leafy Giardini della Biennale gardens. Here, the Venetian Lagoon unfolds its daily theater. Rooms and suites feel less like hotel accommodations and more like the private chambers of a Venetian collector. The luxurious Exclusive lagoon-view damasco suite captures uninterrupted vistas of the waterways. The crowning roof terrace suite offers perhaps the most coveted vantage point. Within these historic walls, the former chapel where Antonio Vivaldi once taught music to orphans has been transformed into the Oriental Bar & Bistrot. Under Gloria Beggiato's family stewardship, the hotel has evolved into something extraordinary — an opulent cabinet of curiosities where every floor reveals a different collection. Vintage Belle Époque evening bags share space with Art Deco feathers, while assemblages of corkscrews and crucifixes speak to the family's eclectic tastes. Sigmund Freud and Marcel Proust are among the illustrious guests of the past.

Description ⚙: Between the grandeur of San Marco and the artistic energy of La Biennale, Ca' di Dio writes its newest chapter in a building that has lived many lives. What once served as a monastery, hospital, and hospice now emerges as an elegant retreat, transformed by Patricia Urquiola's vision in autumn 2021. The designer's touch honors the building's soul while creating spaces that speak to modern sensibilities, all while framing mesmerizing views of the Venetian lagoon. Spread across three buildings with 430 windows capturing Venice's changing light, the 66 rooms and suites tell their stories of contemporary Italian design meeting Venetian artistry. Fifteen rooms face the San Marco basin directly. The Altana Suite's private terrace offers 360-degree views sweeping from San Giorgio Island across the lagoon's expanse. Urquiola's vision unfolds through Molteni&C furnishings and jewel-bright Murano glass lamps. VERO Restaurant extends dining to the lagoon's edge, while Essentia Restaurant transforms a tranquil courtyard into summer's most coveted tables. Alchemia Bar draws guests and locals with cocktails celebrating local ingredients. The Pura spa offers a Turkish steam room and sauna.

Description ⚙: San Clemente Palace Venice is a five-star hotel on the private island of San Clemente, a ten-minute complimentary shuttle boat ride from Piazza San Marco. The property spans 15 acres on a 900-year-old island that includes a 12th-century church, botanical gardens, a 1.5 km jogging path, tennis courts, and a putting green. The hotel has 170 rooms and suites in beautifully restored monastery buildings with high Venetian ceilings and traditional décor. Views from the lagoon-facing rooms extend over the water to the full Venice skyline: the Grand Canal palazzo sequence, the dome of Santa Maria della Salute, San Giorgio Maggiore, and the Campanile. The San Clemente Suite has an almost complete wall of windows over the laguna; Grand Deluxe Lagoon View and Deluxe Lagoon View rooms offer the same panorama; the Laguna Suites are dedicated lagoon-facing accommodation. Insieme Restaurant serves breakfast with views of Venice; Acquerello Restaurant includes a terrace overlooking the private dock and the laguna; La Dolce Restaurant operates poolside throughout the season. The outdoor pool sits in the gardens with the city's profile visible across the water. The Longevity Spa offers comprehensive wellness treatments. The hotel operated as San Clemente Palace Kempinski until 2025, when it became fully independent.

Description ⚙: Sina Palazzo Sant'Angelo is a boutique hotel on the Grand Canal in Venice's San Marco district, occupying a late-19th-century palazzo positioned between the Rialto Bridge and St. Mark's Square, with the Accademia Bridge and La Fenice Opera House both within ten minutes on foot. The property has 26 rooms and suites, individually furnished in 18th-century Venetian style with silk wall coverings, ornate furniture, marble bathrooms, and hydromassage tubs. Canal-facing rooms look out over the Grand Canal and the Palazzo Pisani-Moretto directly opposite. The Deluxe Suites (32 sq m) are the recommended category, with a privileged view of the Grand Canal and some with small private balconies. The bar overlooks the Grand Canal and has a small outdoor terrace directly on the water — a rare position between the Rialto and Accademia bridges. The wood-panelled breakfast room has windows on a lateral canal; al fresco breakfast is served in the garden courtyard. The hotel has a private dock on the Grand Canal. The Sant'Angelo vaporetto stop is directly adjacent. Member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World.

Description ⚙: In Venice's ancient Cannaregio district, The Venice Venice Hotel makes a striking statement from its perch on the Grand Canal. Housed in the 13th-century Ca' da Mosto, one of the city's oldest palazzos, this avant-garde property was conceived by Alessandro Gallo — co-founder of Golden Goose and former artistic director of the Biennale's Venice Pavilion — as the first venture for his eRose lifestyle brand. Inside, architect Alessandro Pedron channels the spirit of Carlo Scarpa, breathing contemporary life into medieval bones. Rooms speak a different language through bold arrangements of glass, metal, and ceramic in place of the usual Venetian brocades. Room 41 frames the Rialto Bridge's timeless arc directly and shares a secret rooftop altanella with neighboring Room 43. Each room includes a chrome bar trolley stocked for impromptu cocktail hours. Additional rooms in the adjacent Ca' Dolfin palazzo echo the same innovative design. The ground floor flows canal-side, where a concept store meets the cocktail bar, a moka bar mingles with the bitter club, and the reception hall opens onto a canal-side terrace. The dining room operates under Venini glass chandeliers and transforms at night into an intimate supper club.

Hotel Tagline: Grand Canal gondolas drift past below, the Dolomites visible beyond Venice's spires from the rooftop.
Summary: Twenty-three rooms in a 15th-century neo-Gothic palazzo on the Grand Canal in Dorsoduro — Proust, Fauré, and D’Annunzio knew the salons. Many rooms face the canal directly; the rooftop Jacuzzi on a clear day takes in the Dolomites beyond Venice’s spires. The room to ask for is the Suite with Terrace.
Description ⚙: Along the Grand Canal in Venice's artistic Dorsoduro district, Hotel Palazzo Stern tells stories of grand salons and creative souls within its neo-Gothic walls. The 15th-century palazzo, transformed by visionaries Raffaele Mainella and Giuseppe Berti, stands as more than just a hotel — it's a chapter of Venice's cultural narrative brought to life. These rooms once echoed with the conversations of Marcel Proust, Gabriel Fauré, and Gabriele D'Annunzio, drawn to the magnetic presence of Ernesta Hierschel Stern's legendary salon. The palazzo's evolution continued under painter Samuel Finkelstein, whose addition of a workshop and exhibition space helped shape the building's distinctive character. The 23 rooms and suites feel less like hotel accommodations and more like private chambers in a noble Venetian home. Many rooms offer front-row seats to the Grand Canal's daily theater, where water buses and gondolas weave their timeless dance below. Mornings begin on the ground floor terrace, where breakfast arrives with Grand Canal views. As sunset approaches, the rooftop terrace reveals its trump card — a Jacuzzi with views stretching beyond Venice's spires to the distant Euganean Hills and, on clear days, the snow-capped Dolomites. The hotel's preservation follows architect Camillo Boito's principles. The Gallerie dell'Accademia and the Peggy Guggenheim Collection are a short walk away.
Address: Sestiere Dorsoduro, 2792/A, 30123 Venezia VE, Italy
Nearest Airports: VCE · Marco Polo · 18 km; TSF · Treviso · 41 km

Description ⚙: Among Venice's newest luxury hotels, Nolinski Venezia writes its own chapter in an unexpected setting — the city's former Borsa, or stock exchange. French hospitality group Evok chose this 1929 architectural gem for its Venetian debut. Design duo Le Coadic/Scotto wove together Art Deco glamour with nostalgic nods to Italy's white telephone films era, preserving original ironwork, restored moldings, and marble features. The ground floor includes a Brunello Cucinelli boutique and the glittering Caffè Nolinski, whose terrace tables offer some of the neighborhood's best people-watching. Rooms and suites on the upper floors wake to iconic vistas of St. Mark's Campanile. Custom Murano glass pieces from Avem scatter light like the lagoon. The Palais Royal restaurant opened in April 2024 under a De Chirico-esque rotunda and arches, serving as Venice's most elegant breakfast venue — with pastries that locals line up for — and an atmospheric dinner destination. Hidden on the third floor, La Colline Spa provides beauty treatments and meditation spaces, with a gold mosaic Jacuzzi.

Worth staying for the upper-floor ocean suites: balcony, separate living room, and a clear read of the Atlantic.
Description ⚙: The Embassy Suites by Hilton Virginia Beach Oceanfront Resort opened in February 2023 as the third and final property of the Cavalier Resort campus. The property offers 157 suites, all with balconies and ocean views from its beachfront stretch of Atlantic Avenue. Each suite arrives with a separate living room, sofa bed, and a complimentary cooked-to-order breakfast. Indoor and outdoor pools, a full-service spa, and two on-site dining venues — Arbuckle's Bar and Grill and TNT, an open-air spot serving margaritas and Mexican cuisine with an oceanfront aspect — are on the property. Guests also have access to the Cavalier Resort's wider amenities, including nine restaurants across the three-hotel campus.

Description ⚙: Sliding open the floor-to-ceiling doors, feeling the maritime breeze, pulling a chair on their room's balcony, and contemplating a spectacular view of the Atlantic are some of the guests' favorite activities when staying at one of Virginia Beach's oceanfront hotels. Among the best stays in Virginia Beach is the beachfront Hampton Inn Virginia Beach Oceanfront North, a very welcoming hotel with high reviews. Does the idea of waking up to a magnificent sunrise over the ocean seduce you? Make sure to book the well-equipped, spacious studio king room, and we promise you won't be disappointed. After a night well slept, guests are invited to enjoy a complimentary breakfast and then decide to spend their relaxing time between the beach and the hotel's indoor pool. The hotel is planted on Virginia Beach Boardwalk, next to Neptune's Park, better known for its gigantic god of the sea statue and for hosting live music shows throughout the year.

The on-site fitness center is open round the clock. The 23rd-floor, Asian-inspired Orion's Roof restaurant offers jaw-dropping views of Virginia Beach and inventive creations. Description ⚙: In case you're considering staying in the best hotel in Virginia Beach, you will likely end up lodging at The Historic Cavalier Hotel and Beach Club. Yes, the views aren't as spectacular as in other nearby hotels, but you can still spot the ocean from some of its 85 luxurious rooms and suites. Getting from The Cavalier Virginia Beach to the beach is only a matter of crossing Atlantic Avenue. The intrinsic relationship between the historic hotel and the ocean continues at the exclusive Beach Club, open from May through October, where guests can freshen up at a gorgeous oceanside infinity pool or unwind at private beach cabanas. After a multi-million dollar renovation that lasted four years, The Historic Cavalier Hotel and Beach Club is shining like never before and has regained its grandeur aura of years past, as the listing on the National Register of Historic Places attests. In the amenities department, guests will indeed feel pampered: the hotel's indoor plunge pool is beautiful, there are three on-site restaurants to choose from, a vast menu of signature treatments in a luxurious spa, a complimentary beach shuttle, and even an on-site distillery, the Tarnished Truth, where tours and tastings are available.

Description ⚙: If you're heading to Virginia Beach, chances are you will be looking to make the most of your much-deserved break. One way to do it is to sunbathe by a panoramic pool with expansive water views; with that in mind, the Delta Hotels Virginia Beach Waterfront Suites is one of the better options in Virginia's favorite seaside destination. The Y-shaped building allows Chesapeake Bay views for all rooms, even if some are only partial. We recommend getting a hold of one of the extensive suites to ensure a memorable stay; waking up to those inviting vistas over the Bay will make you want to jump out of bed and head to the private beach in no time. One of the hotel's highlights is its Tides Coastal Kitchen, where guests can enjoy expansive bay views and savor some of the region's most sought-after delicacies, which include Lynnhaven oysters and soft shell crabs. A short drive from the hotel is Cape Henry Lighthouse, an 18th-century lighthouse commissioned by George Washington.

Description ⚙: The Moxy Virginia Beach Oceanfront opened in 2023 at 1201 Atlantic Avenue and has since collected the LIV Hospitality Design Award 2025 and a Gold Key Awards nomination. The 134 rooms run compact and deliberate: platform beds with built-in drawer storage, walls of hooks in place of closets, bleached-wood floors, and balconies or large windows in oceanfront-facing rooms. The outdoor saltwater pool deck faces the Atlantic directly, and Bar Moxy — the hotel's all-day, all-night bar — anchors the lobby-to-beach connection. The Belvedere South diner on the ground floor runs a deliberately nostalgic American breakfast and brunch format that has drawn a local following since opening. Room selection matters more at the Moxy than at the taller tower properties: oceanfront rooms deliver unobstructed Atlantic views; city-facing rooms face the street.

The beachfront Ocean 27 restaurant, open during the warmer weather, is a lively place to snack and end another perfect day by the beach.

Description ⚙: When staying in Virginia Beach, one thing is for sure: sooner or later, you'll get your toes in the sand. To make this inevitability easier, picking a beachfront hotel like the DoubleTree by Hilton Oceanfront Virginia Beach proves wise. As you soak in the unobstructed ocean vistas from your room's balcony, thoughts of experiencing the local lifestyle may arise. Some of your options will be to take a refreshing dip in the ocean, cycle along the 3.2 miles of Virginia Beach Oceanfront Bike Path, or visit the nearby and impressive Virginia Aquarium & Marine Science Center. Back in the hotel, a vast list of services and amenities, which include free parking, a fitness center, an indoor pool, and a romantic, on-site oceanfront restaurant, will guarantee a pleasant stay.

On the pool side, the property runs both an indoor pool with hot tub and Station 10, a seasonal outdoor pool bar open April through October. Meet the Hilton Vacation Club Ocean Beach Club Virginia Beach, mainly catering to families staying longer and requiring more space. The large-sized hotel offers two and three-bedroom accommodations, some equipped with a fully-functional kitchen and offering fabulous balconies overlooking the beach. On one of the hotel's highest floors, there is a gym with sweeping ocean views, distracting you from the 'no pain, no gain' mindset. Also worth a mention are the two seaside pools, which are particularly popular among kids and a pleasant alternative for those who struggle to face the often cold waters of the North Atlantic.

Description ⚙: On Lafayette Square directly across from the White House, The Hay-Adams opened in 1928 on the former site of the homes of statesman John Hay and historian Henry Adams. Private balconies on the White House-facing side frame the North Lawn, the Washington Monument, and the spire of St. John's Church. The Lafayette restaurant is a Washington institution for power breakfast and Sunday brunch; the Off the Record bar is the capital's most storied political gathering point. Les Cles d'Or concierges arrange monument tours and dining reservations.

Hotel Tagline: All 75 rooms face the open Pacific, and winter storms are the main event.
Summary: When the first November storm reaches Chesterman Beach, all 75 rooms turn into front-row seats — floor-to-ceiling glass, a fireplace burning, the open Pacific rolling past driftwood and cedar. A view certified by The Most Perfect View, in storm season and summer calm alike.
Description ⚙:
On a rocky outcrop at the north end of Chesterman Beach, with old-growth rainforest behind and nothing but open Pacific ahead — the next landfall west is Japan — the Wickaninnish Inn keeps all 75 rooms facing the water. Glass runs floor to ceiling, a fireplace burns in every room, and the balconies hang over the tide line. The Pointe Restaurant wraps a 240-degree arc of sea behind glass; the Ancient Cedars Spa treats guests in rooms cantilevered above the surf.

Winter is the signature season. From November to February, storm fronts stack swells against the beach, and the Inn hands out rain gear so guests can walk into the weather before watching it from the fireside. This is one of the places where storm watching was turned into a reason to travel — and the view that carries it holds The Most Perfect View certification, verified across rooms, restaurant and shoreline.
Address: 500 Osprey Ln, Tofino, BC V0R 3A0, Canada
Nearest Airports: YAZ · Tofino · 15 km

Hotel Tagline: Beach houses sit right on Cox Bay sand, a step from the surf.
Summary: Step off your deck and the next footprint lands on Cox Bay sand. Suites and beach houses face the surf break that made Tofino famous, so the Pacific fills the windows from bed, kitchen and hot tub alike — waves arriving all day, sunsets closing the show.
Description ⚙:
Cox Bay made Tofino Canada's wave-riding capital, and Pacific Sands spreads along the full length of it: suites and multi-bedroom beach houses directly behind the sand — no road, no lawn, just deck, dune grass and breakers. The bay faces almost due west, so sunsets land straight in the windows, and the surf-in, surf-out layout puts the walk from bed to break at under a minute.

Inside, the argument continues: full kitchens for long stays, gas fireplaces for storm nights, hot tubs on the decks with the ocean still in frame. The Surfside Grill hands out fish tacos beside the beach path, and when the Pacific turns violent in winter, the same west-facing windows that catch the sunsets take the full force of the show.
Address: 1421 Pacific Rim Hwy, Tofino, BC V0R 3A0, Canada
Nearest Airports: YAZ · Tofino · 12 km

Hotel Tagline: The timber Great Room points its glass straight at the break.
Summary: Floor-to-ceiling windows run the length of the Great Room, putting the full sweep of Cox Bay on display from armchair height. Guestrooms and cottages carry the same view onto private balconies, close enough to the break that surfers drift past your morning coffee.
Description ⚙:
The Great Room sets the tone here: a timber-framed hall with glass running the width of the building, armchairs and a river-stone fireplace pointed at the break. It belongs to Long Beach Lodge, anchored at the southern end of Cox Bay behind a shield of salt-sprayed pines, and it may be the best seat on the west coast for watching surfers work a wave — or a storm dismantle one.

Upstairs, lodge rooms share the orientation from balconies of their own; two-bedroom cottages sit in the rainforest fringe with hot tubs on the deck. The resort runs its own Surf Club — instructors, wetsuits, a heated outdoor training pool — and the kitchen plates Pacific Northwest cooking a few metres from the tide line. The glass takes the spray so you don't have to.
Address: 1441 Pacific Rim Hwy, Tofino, BC V0R 2Z0, Canada

Hotel Tagline: From the Malahat ridge, every window looks down the Finlayson Arm fjord.
Summary: High on the Malahat ridge, the resort looks straight down Finlayson Arm — a green fjord threading between Douglas firs, with eagles riding the thermals below the balconies. Rooms, terraces and the spa all face the same long drop, sharpest at first light.
Description ⚙:
Finlayson Arm reads more like Norway than the usual idea of Vancouver Island — a narrow, forest-walled fjord — and Villa Eyrie looks straight down the length of it from the Malahat ridge, 350 metres up. Rooms and suites face the drop; so do the Italian-leaning restaurant and the spa's heated outdoor pool. Bald eagles routinely ride the thermals below eye level.

Mornings are the performance: fog pools in the Arm at dawn and burns off in ribbons as the sun clears the ridge, a show best taken from bed. Victoria sits forty minutes south and the Malahat SkyWalk five minutes away, but the resort's whole argument is the view you never have to leave the room for.
Address: 600 Ebadora Ln, Malahat, BC V0R 2L0, Canada
Nearest Airports: YYJ · Victoria International · 50 km; YCD · Nanaimo · 69 km

Summary: The heated mineral pools sit at the seawall's edge, so you soak eye-level with the Salish Sea while Mount Baker floats on the horizon. Oceanfront rooms and the spa terrace share the same channel view — sailboats, seals and, on clear days, that snow-capped cone.
Description ⚙:
Heated mineral pools set into the rocks at the ocean's edge: that is the best idea at the Oak Bay Beach Hotel, a Tudor-styled landmark on Victoria's eastern seawall, rebuilt in 2012 around it. Soaking there puts your eye line level with the Salish Sea, sailboats mid-channel and, on clear days, Mount Baker's snow cone floating on the horizon. Oceanfront rooms and suites carry the same channel view from their balconies.

The Boathouse Spa books treatments on a terrace over the water and David's Kitchen handles the fine dining — but the soul of the place is the Snug, the hotel's sea-windowed pub since 1954, where the pint comes with the same horizon the pools have.
Address: 1175 Beach Dr, Victoria, BC V8S 2N2, Canada

Summary: Every room comes with a balcony aimed at Victoria's Inner Harbour, where floatplanes land between water taxis and the Parliament dome catches the evening light. Below, a Japanese garden runs down to the water — the quiet corner of a working harbour.
Description ⚙:
A private peninsula on the quiet side of Victoria's Inner Harbour is the whole premise. At Inn at Laurel Point, every room in both wings comes with a balcony on the water, and the harbour works while you watch: floatplanes landing in lanes between water taxis, ferries turning at the point, the Parliament dome catching light across the water. Below, a Japanese garden with two ponds runs down to the shoreline path.

The Laurel wing's curved architecture gives its corner suites a double exposure, and AURA restaurant pairs Pacific Rim cooking with a terrace at water level. Few city-harbour hotels manage this combination — a working port kept picturesque, and quiet, by just enough distance.

Hotel Tagline: Victoria's grand hotel has faced the Inner Harbour head-on since 1908.
Summary: Since 1908 the Empress has faced the Inner Harbour head-on, ivy-covered and unmoved. Harbour-view rooms overlook the causeway, the moored yachts and the Parliament buildings, lit each night by thousands of bulbs — Victoria's front porch, seen from its grandest address.
Description ⚙:
Since 1908, Victoria's Inner Harbour has had a fixed point — ivy-covered, château-roofed, impossible to miss. The city effectively poses around the Empress. Harbour-view rooms and Fairmont Gold suites overlook the causeway, the moored yachts and the Parliament buildings, outlined each night in thousands of bulbs; afternoon tea in the Lobby Lounge has run for over a century with that view through the windows.

A 2017 restoration lightened the interiors without touching the bones — hand-carved mouldings, the Q bar's painted ceiling, gardens holding the building apart from the street. The view here is double-sided: the harbour from your window, and the Empress itself when you walk the causeway back at dusk.
Address: 721 Government St, Victoria, BC V8W 1W5, Canada

Hotel Tagline: The picture windows do one job: keep the Yasaka Pagoda above Kyoto's tiled rooftops from sunrise to illumination.
Summary: Twelve centuries of skyline, one window. Park Hyatt Kyoto's view rooms put the five-story Yasaka Pagoda dead ahead above the Higashiyama townscape — close enough to count the tiers, far enough to watch the whole city turn amber at dusk.
Description ⚙: Park Hyatt Kyoto opened in October 2019 on the Higashiyama hillside, beside Kodai-ji and the stone-paved Ninenzaka slope that climbs toward Kiyomizu-dera. The 70 rooms and suites are kept deliberately low against the hill, and the view categories aim their picture windows straight at the five-story Yasaka Pagoda, which rises above the tiled machiya roofs with mountains closing the horizon behind. At dusk the pagoda is illuminated, and from bed it sits framed left of center over the darkening townscape. The view repeats in public: on the fourth floor, the teppan counter at Yasaka faces a panoramic glass wall over the same rooftops, and Bar Kohaku next to it is timed for sunset. Downhill, KYOTO BISTRO opens directly onto Ninenzaka itself, so the streetscape you watched from above becomes the one you walk through.
Address: 京都市東山区高台寺, 360 桝屋町 東山区 京都市 京都府 605-0826, Japan

Hotel Tagline: The five-story pagoda of Hōkan-ji stands directly across from the K36 rooftop terrace, lit up every night.
Summary: Hōkan-ji's pagoda is the fixed point here: it rises from Higashiyama's low tiled roofs directly beyond the rail of the K36 rooftop, holds the lounge windows by day, and glows lamplit in the room glass after dark.
Description ⚙: Halfway up Kiyomizu-zaka, classrooms from 1933 became 48 guest rooms in 2020 — and the best of them look straight at the Yasaka Pagoda. The wooden five-story tower of Hōkan-ji rises through floor-to-ceiling windows above Higashiyama's tiled roofs, visible from bed in the pagoda-facing rooms and framed centrally from the fourth-floor terrace of K36 The Bar & Rooftop. The guest lounge holds a direct, front-on view of the pagoda over coffee or an evening glass. In winter the scene turns rarer still: snow on the pagoda's five roofs, seen across the hotel's own courtyard. The Panoramic Suite adds a second landmark, its balcony reaching past the pagoda to Kyoto Tower. A Leading Hotels of the World member, but the membership that matters is the view's.

Hotel Tagline: An entire room category aimed at Kyoto Tower, and a 15th-floor sky lounge pouring drinks over the same skyline.
Summary: Kyoto Tower stands directly across the station forecourt, and this hotel sells the sight by name: a renovated Tower View category on the upper floors, where the white shaft and its lit observation deck hold the window with mountain ridgelines stacked behind.
Description ⚙: Hotel Granvia Kyoto occupies the upper floors of the Kyoto Station Building, with 541 rooms set between the 7th and 15th floors — high enough that the city reads as a plain of low rooftops running to the mountains. The renovated Tower View category faces Kyoto Tower head-on across the station, its windows expanded up to the eaves so the white, lighthouse-shaped landmark and the ridgelines of the five mountains fill the frame. The hotel itself recommends returning shortly before sunset: the twilight transition over the tower lasts roughly thirty minutes and is the room's daily event. On a clear day, the Yasaka Pagoda is legible in the distance among the Higashiyama rooftops. Non-guests of the view rooms aren't shut out — the Sky Lounge Southern Court on the 15th floor serves dinner and cocktails over the same skyline, and Granvia Floor guests get the 15th-floor Granvia Lounge with its own outlook.

Hotel Tagline: Kyoto Tower appears framed in the entrance noren before it fills the Tower View suites at dusk.
Summary: The view announces itself before check-in: through the gap in the entrance noren and up the exterior steps, Kyoto Tower's white shaft and red-lit spire stand framed against the night sky. Inside, the Kanra Junior Suite (Tower View) puts the same silhouette in the window from bed.
Description ⚙: A former school building on a narrow Shimogyo street became, in 2010, one of Kyoto's first serious design hotels — and its 2016 expansion to 68 rooms formalised the view with a category of its own. The Kanra Junior Suite (Tower View) looks straight at Kyoto Tower, the white-and-blue illuminated spire clearing the low skyline through the right-side window at dusk. A small suite adds an internal garden and outdoor bath with the tower and Higashi Honganji Temple both in sight; the temple itself is one block south, Kyoto Station twelve minutes away on foot. Rooms follow the elongated machiya plan, tatami and cypress baths throughout. Public spaces keep the tone interior — a café lounge off the lobby, wood-fired Italian at THE KITCHEN KANRA, wagyu teppanyaki at Hanaroku — leaving the tower to the suites and to the entrance corridor, where it stands framed in the gap of the noren against the night.
Address: 190 Kitamachi, Shimogyo Ward, Kyoto, 600-8176, Japan

Hotel Tagline: Kyoto's only revolving restaurant crowns the 14th floor, and Kyoto Tower comes around every 90 minutes.
Summary: On the 14th floor, Kyoto's only revolving restaurant turns a full circle every 90 minutes — long enough for Kyoto Tower to slide past your table and, on a clear day, for the five-story Yasaka Pagoda to appear above the Higashiyama rooftops before dessert.
Description ⚙: West of Kyoto Station by seven minutes on foot, the Rihga Royal has anchored this corner of Shimogyo since 1969 — 489 rooms, 14 floors, and one dining room that refuses to hold still. Kyoto's only revolving restaurant occupies the top floor, and its slow 90-minute turn is a scheduled tour of the eastern skyline: Kyoto Tower first, near enough to dominate the glass, then the Yasaka Pagoda standing five stories above the Higashiyama rooftops. At breakfast the panorama arrives with morning light on the hills; at dinner the tower burns orange over the city grid while the pagoda thins to a lit silhouette. East-facing rooms on the upper floors, refreshed in the 2016 renovation, keep the same bearings without the rotation. The station is close enough that the view includes the trains that brought you.
Address: Japan, 〒600-8237 Kyoto, Shimogyo Ward, Taimatsuchō, 1番地
Nearest Airports: ITM · Osaka Itami · 45 km

Hotel Tagline: Suite balconies hang over the Hozu River, and 17 private onsens steam facing the Arashiyama ridgeline.
Summary: The Hozu River runs straight past Café Hassui's terrace, and from that thatched-roof pavilion — built in 1910 as a retreat for poets — the forested Arashiyama hills fill the entire frame. Upstairs, balconied suites put the same river and ridgeline outside the glass, no road or rooftop in between.
Description ⚙: Opened in 2015 as the first Luxury Collection hotel in Japan, Suiran is a 39-room ryokan-style property on the Hozu riverbank at the western edge of Kyoto, where Arashiyama's forested hills stand directly across the water. Rooms behind floor-to-ceiling windows look onto gardens, river and mountains; select suites, including the Arashiyama View Suite, add private balconies over the water, and 17 rooms hold open-air onsen baths drawn from the local spring. The closest seat to the river is Café Hassui, a century-old thatched pavilion at the water's edge, where a complimentary evening aperitif — the nightly Arashiyama Delight — is served against the riverside panorama, and winter brings snow-capped mountains into the frame. Dinner at Kyo-Suiran, the 1899 Meiji villa turned restaurant, comes with unobstructed views of the garden and the Arashiyama hills. The bamboo grove and Togetsu-kyo bridge are within walking distance, best taken at dawn before the day-trippers arrive.
Address: Japan, 〒616-8385 Kyoto, Ukyo Ward, Sagatenryūji Susukinobabachō, 翠嵐ラグジュアリーコレクションホテル京都
Nearest Airports: ITM · Osaka Itami · 52 km

Hotel Tagline: The Kamogawa flows past the Lobby Lounge glass, and select suites open balconies above the same water.
Summary: The Kamogawa runs directly below the windows here: Grand Deluxe Kamogawa rooms face the river and the Higashiyama mountains behind it, and because the building rises only five storeys, the water stays close — this is a river view at river scale, not from a tower.
Description ⚙: From a Grand Deluxe Kamogawa room, the sequence out the window is fixed: the river below, the far bank, then the Higashiyama mountains closing the frame. The Ritz-Carlton, Kyoto has held this position on the Kamogawa's bank at Nijo Ohashi since 2014, with 134 rooms in a building of only five storeys — low enough that the water reads as foreground, not map. Luxury Rooms carry floor-to-ceiling windows onto river or mountains, and select suites open onto private balconies above the bank. Downstairs, the Lobby Lounge faces the water, putting the river behind every Pierre Hermé afternoon tea. La Locanda, the four Mizuki counters (tempura holds a Michelin star) and The Bar complete the floor plan, and the riverside path outside leads into Gion on foot.
Address: Japan, 〒604-0902 Kyoto, Nakagyo Ward, Hokodenchō, ５４３ 鴨川二条大橋畔

Hotel Tagline: Nineteen rooms on the Kamo riverbank, and the City rooms catch Kyoto Tower's white spire through a corner window.
Summary: Through the corner window of the City rooms, Kyoto Tower's white spire stands clear above Shimogyo's low rooftops — an unexpected Tower sightline from a 19-room Design Hotels property on the banks of the Kamo River.
Description ⚙: Between the Kamo River and a warren of narrow Shimogyo lanes, Genji Kyoto packs three views into five floors and 19 rooms. Facing east, nine river rooms open onto balconies over the Kamogawa with the Higashiyama mountains behind. Facing the city, the compact City rooms hold a different prize: Kyoto Tower, its white spire framed in the corner window against a skyline that stays deliberately low. Everyone shares the rooftop Sky Forest Garden — a planted terrace on the top level where breakfast, light meals and sunset drinks face the river and the mountains. The building is a 2022 reinterpretation of the machiya townhouse by Kyoto-based architect Geoffrey P. Moussas, and the ground-floor Genji Lounge looks onto a contemporary Zen garden by Marc Peter Keane. Kiyomizu-Gojo station is six minutes away on foot.
Address: 362-3 Hashidonochō, Shimogyo Ward, Kyoto, 600-8113, Japan
Nearest Airports: ITM · Osaka Itami · 51 km

Hotel Tagline: One 3-metre tub on the third floor looks straight at Hōkan-ji's five wooden storeys.
Summary: The best seat in this hotel is a bathtub. Tau-yasaka, the reservation-only private bath on the third floor, holds the five-story Yasaka Pagoda in its window — a 3-metre tub filled with seasonal yuzu or pine waters, and 46 metres of 1440-era timber rising above the machiya rooftops while you soak.
Description ⚙: The Yasaka Pagoda — rebuilt in 1440, 46 metres of dark timber — is the emblem of Higashiyama, and this hotel positions its single best window on it in an unusual place: a bath. On the third floor, the private tub Tau-yasaka faces the pagoda across 350 metres of low tiled rooftops, bookable in 50-minute turns with seasonal waters drawn from the hotel's Kyoto Kiyomizu Onsen source, introduced in 2024. It is a shared facility rather than a room view, which is precisely the appeal — the pagoda arrives framed, private and paid for by the slot. The rest of the house is a 38-room modern ryokan on the walking route to Kiyomizu-dera, five minutes downhill from the temple gates, with some rooms opening to terraces over the Kyoto cityscape. Dinner is at Dining Kiyomizu Saryo on site; the Otowa Living lounge shares the third floor with the bath.
Address: 4-chōme-200 Kiyomizu, Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto, 605-0862, Japan
Nearest Airports: ITM · Osaka Itami · 51 km

Hotel Tagline: Banyan Tree's 2024 Kyoto debut looks down the Higashiyama slope to the Yasaka Pagoda, framed in shoji.
Summary: The window does the framing at this 2024 opening — shoji screens pull apart on the Yasaka Pagoda over Higashiyama's rooftops, seen from above and at a distance that keeps the whole city in the same glass.
Description ⚙: A short climb above the lanes that lead to Kiyomizu-dera, this hotel occupies the ground of the former Hotel Ryozen, rebuilt as Banyan Tree's first Japanese property with 52 rooms in August 2024. Height is what the location buys: the city-view rooms sit above the rooftop line of Higashiyama, so the Yasaka Pagoda appears in the window from above, its five tiers clear of the machiya roofs, with the flat grid of Kyoto stretching beyond. Shoji screens frame the scene from the bed. The rest of the hotel looks the other way — into a bamboo forest and onto the Kengo Kuma Noh stage, the only one inside a Kyoto hotel, visible from the 48-seat Ryozen restaurant at breakfast and from the Onsen Retreat rooms' private baths. Gion and Kodai-ji are within walking distance downhill; the pagoda you walked past on the way up is the one waiting in the glass.
Address: Japan, 〒605-0861 Kyoto, Higashiyama Ward, Seikanji Ryōzanchō, 7番地

Hotel Tagline: The Kamo River passes the front door, and the 10th-floor Grand Café FAUCHON looks over it to the Higashiyama mountains.
Summary: Paris's Fauchon picked a Kyoto riverbank for its only hotel outside France. Higashiyama View rooms on floors 7 to 9 look across the Kamogawa to the eastern mountains, and breakfast in the top-floor restaurant faces the same river.
Description ⚙: Fauchon's second hotel in the world, opened in 2021, stands on the Kamo River in Shimogyo-ku, steps from the historic Matsubara Bridge, with Gion and Shijo Kawaramachi within walking distance. River-facing rooms look straight across the Kamogawa to the Higashiyama range, and the dedicated Higashiyama View categories — Classic through Prestige Suite — occupy floors 7 to 9. The real reveal comes at check-in, which takes place on the 10th floor: the lobby lounge keeps its sofas by the windows, and the Grand Café FAUCHON next to it serves French cuisine over the river and the mountains. Le Bar FAUCHON shares the same top floor for sunset over the city. A Leading Hotels of the World member, it is the boutique river option among Kyoto's luxury addresses.
Address: 406 Nanbachō, Shimogyo Ward, Kyoto, 600-8027, Japan
Nearest Airports: ITM · Osaka Itami · 51 km

Hotel Tagline: Every soak in this building — public, private or footbath — points east at the Higashiyama hills.
Summary: Nine floors above the Shijo-Kawaramachi crossing, a hot-spring footbath runs under the rooftop bar counter, and the panorama it faces reaches across the Kamogawa to the Higashiyama hills — Yasaka Pagoda in the frame.
Description ⚙: The building sits on Kawaramachi-dori in the middle of Kyoto's busiest shopping district, beside Hankyu Kyoto-kawaramachi Station, and everything worth looking at happens on its east side and its roof. Check-in is on the 9th floor, where the Sora Niwa Terrace rooftop lounge serves coffee by day and drinks by night at counter seats with a natural hot-spring footbath running beneath them; the panorama crosses the Kamogawa to Higashiyama, with the Yasaka Pagoda among the landmarks named in the frame. On the same top floor, the Yasaka-no-Yu open-air bath — with a 1.2-metre-deep section for standing immersion — holds the identical view from the water. The Bettei, the elite wing opened in June 2022, adds 32 rooms that each have a private open-air bath fed by the hotel's own spring on their own terrace, facing the Higashiyama townscape. Dinner is kaiseki at the in-house restaurant Higashiyama, named after the hills outside.
Address: 324番地 Inarichō, Shimogyo Ward, Kyoto, 600-8022, Japan
Nearest Airports: ITM · Osaka Itami · 51 km

Hotel Tagline: Japan's first Six Senses keeps the skyline low in its floor-to-ceiling glass — treetops, tiled roofs, and Kyoto Tower in the distance.
Summary: Japan's first Six Senses opened in April 2024 beside the 16th-century Toyokuni Shrine, and its city-view rooms read Kyoto in layers — treetops, tiled roofs, mountain ridgelines — with Kyoto Tower a distant white pin holding the skyline about two kilometers out.
Description ⚙: Distance is the point at this address: Kyoto keeps its skyline low, so from the city-view rooms the eye travels uninterrupted across treetops and tiled roofs to the Higashiyama hills, and Kyoto Tower's white spire is the lone vertical on the horizon, roughly two kilometers off. The hotel — the first Six Senses in Japan, opened April 2024 — sits beside the 16th-century Toyokuni Shrine in Southern Higashiyama, its 81 rooms and suites arranged around an inner courtyard garden. Courtyard and Garden categories look inward and toward the shrine; the Superior, Deluxe and Junior Suite City rooms take the skyline through floor-to-ceiling glass. The rooftop lounge on the fourth floor is the public version of that view, strongest at sunset. Above it, a 238-square-meter three-bedroom penthouse with an adjacent rooftop terrace was unveiled in 2026, while Sekki, the micro-seasonal restaurant, and the Nine Tails bar hold the garden levels below.
Address: 431 Myōhōin Maekawachō, Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto, 605-0932, Japan
Nearest Airports: ITM · Osaka Itami · 51 km

Hotel Tagline: An 800-year-old pond garden fills the windows here, with the Higashiyama Mountains closing the frame.
Summary: The view this hotel sells is 800 years older than the building: Shakusui-en, a pond garden mentioned in The Tale of the Heike, fills the windows of the garden-facing rooms with the Higashiyama Mountains rising behind it.
Description ⚙: Most Kyoto hotels borrow their views; this one owns its view outright. Shakusui-en, the 800-year-old ikeniwa at the property's centre, is what the garden-facing rooms, the balconied fourth-floor Heritage Garden rooms and the omakase counter at Sushi Ginza Onodera all look at — cherry blossoms in spring, maples in autumn, herons and carp year-round. The setting is the foot of the Higashiyama Mountains in the temple district, beside the 12th-century Myoho-in Temple, and the garden's west-to-east length draws the eye straight to the ridgeline. Upper-floor Kyoto View rooms and the residential suites face outward instead, over the city. The Shakusui-tei teahouse stands inside the garden for tea ceremonies, and The Lounge & Bar on lobby level rounds out the public spaces. In 2025 Condé Nast Traveler readers ranked it the #6 hotel in Japan.
Address: 445-3 Myōhōin Maekawachō, Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto, 605-0932, Japan
Nearest Airports: ITM · Osaka Itami · 51 km

Hotel Tagline: A Keage hillside held since 1890, with 266 rooms facing the Higashiyama mountains and a city that stayed low.
Summary: Where the Lake Biwa Canal enters Kyoto, at the foot of Mount Kacho, this 1890 grande dame looks downhill over gardens laid out by Ogawa Jihei VII to a city that stayed low — so the view from the north-facing rooms still ends at mountains, not buildings.
Description ⚙: The Westin Miyako Kyoto stands on the Keage hillside in northern Higashiyama, the spot where the Lake Biwa Canal enters the city, and it has occupied it since 1890. North-side deluxe rooms and the Heian-kyo View suites look across the hotel's own Japanese gardens — the Aoi-den garden was designed by Ogawa Jihei VII — to the low-rise Okazaki district around Nanzen-ji and Heian Shrine, with the Kitayama ridgelines marking the far edge. The 130th-anniversary renovation halved the count to 266 rooms and pushed the average size from 35 to about 50 square meters, so the windows got the space they deserve. Downstairs, the all-day dining RAQOU frames the same mountain-and-city panorama over breakfast, and Spa KACHO's Keage onsen looks onto the gardens. The 12-room Kasui-en annex, Togo Murano's 1959 sukiya masterpiece reborn in 2020, sits within its own garden with hot-spring baths in every room.
Address: Japan, 〒1 Kyoto, Higashiyama Ward, Awadaguchi Kachōchō, JP 605-0052, Keage Sanjo, Higashiyaman-Ku

Hotel Tagline: Some windows hold a UNESCO castle gate; the other side of the hotel holds its own 1,300 m² garden.
Summary: The window seat in the 50 m² Nijo Room points at one thing only — the Higashi Otemon Gate of Nijo Castle, built in 1603, illuminated each night just across the road.
Description ⚙: Few hotels can put a UNESCO World Heritage Site in a bedroom window at street width; this one can, from exactly the rooms named for it. The Nijo Room (50 m²) and Nijo Suite (112 m²) face the Higashi Otemon Gate of Nijo-jo Castle, constructed in 1603, with the corner watchtower visible beside it and the walls lit each evening. The building itself sits on the 250-year-old Kyoto estate of the Mitsui family, and its second view is its own: a 1,300 m² landscape garden by Shunsaku Miyagi fills the ground-floor core, watched from the tables of TOKI, FORNI, The Garden Bar and the Shiki-no-ma pavilion. Upstairs, garden rooms overlook the cherry tree and pond, while other rooms face the city or the surrounding mountains. An underground onsen, fed by a natural spring beneath the property, trades views for steam.
Address: 284 Nijōaburanokōjichō, Nakagyo Ward, Kyoto, 604-0051, Japan

Hotel Tagline: Kerzner's twin 1970s towers still face the Indian Ocean — now with a R250 million makeover underway.
Summary: Sol Kerzner raised these twin towers on Durban's beachfront in the 1970s, and the Indian Ocean is still the whole point — 734 rooms trading on the same view, with a new pool deck going up on top of the 33-storey Maharani tower.
Description ⚙: The Elangeni & Maharani stands at 63 Snell Parade, metres from North Beach on Durban's Golden Mile, its two towers merged into a single 734-room hotel in 2012. Sea-facing rooms look straight down the palm-lined promenade, with the pier to one side and the surf breaking directly below. Three pools carry the same view at different heights — most plainly from the rooftop deck, where the beachfront runs past the glass balustrade. Sundowners at the Panorama Bar keep the ocean in frame, while Lingela on the ground floor of the Elangeni tower and breakfast at Daruma or The Grill Jichana handle the rest of the day. A R250 million, three-year refurbishment began with the first rooms, the Elangeni tower's exterior and a new pool deck atop the 33-storey Maharani tower; the hotel stays open throughout.
Address: 63 Snell Parade, North Beach, Durban, 4001, South Africa

Hotel Tagline: Seven floors above the Golden Mile, the rooftop pool serves sundowners over New Pier and the open Indian Ocean.
Summary: Since 1911 The Edward has held the same address on OR Tambo Parade — and the same subject: half of its 131 rooms look straight over North Beach, where New Pier runs into the surf and container ships queue on the horizon for Durban's port.
Description ⚙: From a sea-facing room on the upper floors, the view reads left to right like a map of Durban's beachfront: palm crowns, the promenade, North Beach, then open Indian Ocean broken only by New Pier and the ships waiting for the harbour. That view belongs to half of the hotel's 131 rooms, some with balconies that put nothing between guest and horizon but a sliding glass door. The address is 149 OR Tambo Parade, the promenade is metres from the entrance, and the building — seven storeys of 1911 Art Deco — sits directly opposite the beach. The sea follows you through the public rooms too: the Brasserie Restaurant dines with ocean views from breakfast to dinner, and the rooftop pool turns the whole Golden Mile into a sundowner backdrop.
Address: 149 Marine Parade, South Beach, Durban, 4001, South Africa

Hotel Tagline: A rooftop infinity pool 20 metres from Battery Beach, with the Golden Mile running south below.
Summary: This is the Golden Mile without the crowd: a solitary tower at the strip's northern end, 20 metres from Battery Beach, where balconies track the paved promenade below and the rooftop bar keeps the sunset view along the coast to itself.
Description ⚙: The address explains the view: 175 Snell Parade, where the Golden Mile runs out of buildings and Battery Beach takes over, 20 metres from the door. Balconies come with most of the 262 rooms, and what they hold is the working length of Durban's beachfront — promenade, palms, the New Pier, surfers in the break — rather than a slot between neighbouring towers. Afternoon tea in the Florida Lounge happens in front of the Indian Ocean, dinner at the Versailles Restaurant keeps the same orientation, and the Blue Dolphin bar covers the evening. The rooftop is the summit of it: an infinity pool over the sand and a bar with sunset views tracking the coastline south, the hotel corridor of the Golden Mile receding toward the Bluff. Suncoast is a 250-metre walk when the promenade calls.
Address: 175 Snell Parade, Marine Parade, North Beach, Durban, 4056, South Africa

Hotel Tagline: Thirty-seven rooms and suites, and every window holds the Golden Mile's sand and surf.
Summary: Above the slot floors of Suncoast Casino, a boutique tower of just 37 rooms and suites turns its back on the games and its glass toward the sea: wide sand, breaking surf, and the Indian Ocean running the length of the Golden Mile below.
Description ⚙: From a treatment table on the ninth floor, the view is the reason to book: sand directly below, the promenade running along it, and the Indian Ocean breaking white against the Golden Mile. That spa — seven treatment rooms and a pool deck facing the sea — crowns a boutique tower of 37 rooms and suites at 20 Battery Beach Road, the northern anchor of Durban's beachfront strip. Every room carries the panorama, and the suites' floor-to-ceiling glass puts the surf at eye level; a handful add balconies. Downstairs, The Hotel Bar serves cocktails beside the pool within earshot of the waves, and Jeera plates Durban-style Indian cooking a floor above the Suncoast Casino. Step out the door and the promenade is right there, running south past North Beach toward uShaka.
Address: 20 Battery Beach Rd, Stamford Hill, Durban, 4001, South Africa

Hotel Tagline: Breakfast on the top floor, the Golden Mile eleven storeys below.
Summary: Breakfast at the Belaire happens eleven storeys up: the Sky Lounge's windows hold the full run of the Golden Mile — palm-lined promenade, breaking surf, the pier — before the first coffee is poured.
Description ⚙: What the windows hold: the paved beachfront promenade with its palms, the sand and breaking surf of North Beach, the pier pushing into the Indian Ocean, and — on clear days — a coastline running from Umhlanga Rocks down to the Bluff. This is the daily view from most of the 124 kitchenette suites at the Belaire, an eleven-storey aparthotel at 151 Snell Parade beside Blue Waters. The same panorama returns each morning in the top-floor Sky Lounge, where the breakfast buffet is set against unobstructed ocean glass. Downstairs, Café Jiran opens onto the sidewalk, with the Golden Mile promenade beginning across the road and Suncoast Casino a six-minute walk south.
Address: 151 Snell Parade, North Beach, Durban, 4056, South Africa

Hotel Tagline: Sea-facing balconies open straight onto the 21-metre uMhlanga Lighthouse, with the Indian Ocean breaking behind it.
Summary: This is the only hotel anywhere that is the official warden of the lighthouse it overlooks — built in November 1954, the striped tower stands directly beside the pool deck, between your sun lounger and the open Indian Ocean.
Description ⚙: The lighthouse came second: it was raised on the rocks in November 1954, after the hotel was already here, and The Oyster Box has served as its official warden ever since. That accident of sequence produced a view no other hotel has — a working, unmanned lighthouse standing metres from the pool deck, with nothing but the Indian Ocean behind it. Sea-facing balconies frame the tower at close range against the water; suites add arched windows and terraces where the surf and the red-topped column share the same glass. Public spaces repeat the composition from different heights: the Ocean Terrace at sea level, where the lighthouse punctuates the horizon over lunch, and the top-floor Lighthouse Bar, which looks down on the beacon and out to open water. Of the hotel's 86 rooms, suites and villas, the sea-facing ones hold the front row.
Address: 2 Lighthouse Rd, Umhlanga Rocks, uMhlanga, 4319, South Africa

Hotel Tagline: South Africa's first five-star hotel, on a clifftop between the Whalebone Pier and the lighthouse since 1964.
Summary: South Africa's first five-star hotel has held the same uMhlanga clifftop since 1964, and all 89 rooms still earn the site: every one has a private balcony facing the open Indian Ocean, with the red-and-white lighthouse standing on the rocks directly below.
Description ⚙: Sunrise happens over the Indian Ocean here, and every one of the 89 balconies faces it — floor-to-ceiling doors in the Junior Suites open straight onto the water, with dolphins passing in the surf and cargo ships tracking the horizon toward Durban. This is South Africa's original five-star hotel, open since 1964 on the clifftop at uMhlanga Rocks, positioned between the Whalebone Pier to one side and the lighthouse to the other. The public spaces share the exposure rather than hoarding it: the heated pool and its lawn of loungers sit at the water's edge, the Vista Terrace handles cocktails with an uninterrupted sea view, and The Sugar Club pairs its dining room with the same stretch of ocean. The lighthouse itself — red top, white base — stands on the rocks just below the terrace, visible between the umbrellas and the surf. There is a private entrance down to the beach when watching stops being enough.
Address: 1 Lighthouse Road uMhlanga Rocks, Umhlanga, Durban, 4320, South Africa

Hotel Tagline: From the sea-view rooms, the Indian Ocean fills the frame and the uMhlanga Lighthouse marks the shore below.
Summary: From the upper floors on Lagoon Drive, the Indian Ocean fills the glass — and on most days, a line of container ships sits parked on the horizon, waiting their turn into Durban harbour. All 206 rooms were built around that view.
Description ⚙: Umhlanga's skyline gained this tower in June 2022, and its viewing platform is the 6th floor: an outdoor infinity pool whose edge dissolves into the Indian Ocean, a pool bar on the deck, and FireLake Grill House & Cocktail Bar serving open-flame cooking beside floor-to-ceiling windows that hold the sea horizon. Above it, the sea-view rooms among the 206 continue the theme up to the 14th floor — glass walls, the coastline and city rooftops in the foreground, open water behind, ships anchored in the distance off Durban harbour. Look carefully among the buildings below and the uMhlanga Lighthouse marks the rocks of the main beach. The hotel occupies 7 Lagoon Drive in the Oceans development, mall attached, promenade a few minutes' walk away.
Address: 7 Lagoon Dr, Umhlanga, Durban, 4320, South Africa

Hotel Tagline: Fourteen floors up on Umhlanga Ridge, the sea-facing rooms watch the town run downhill to the Indian Ocean.
Summary: South Africa's first Hilton Garden Inn trades the beachfront for altitude: 203 rooms stacked inside the glass Umhlanga Arch since November 2020, reading the coastline from above with the ocean holding the horizon.
Description ⚙: Set back on Umhlanga Ridge at 1 Ncondo Place, this is not a beachfront hotel — it is a 14-storey tower inside the glass Umhlanga Arch, about two kilometres inland from the lighthouse, and the view works on distance. Each of the 203 rooms carries a single pane of performance glass, and on the higher sea-facing floors that pane frames the rooftops of uMhlanga sloping down to the Indian Ocean and a long, hazy horizon. The building was deliberately angled so rooms look up and down the coastline rather than at a single stretch of sand. Up top, the heated outdoor pool points the same way, its far edge giving onto open water, while the Back Yard rooftop bar serves drinks over the same panorama. At street level, Together & Co restaurant and the eight-vendor Legacy Yard food hall anchor the Arch's high street. Open since November 2020, it remains South Africa's first Hilton Garden Inn.
Address: 1 Ncondo Pl, Umhlanga Ridge, uMhlanga, 4320, South Africa
